news.n_title: To prevent BJP 3.0: Chandrashekhar Azad, Owaisi tie up, to contest all UP seats
news.n_description: Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM and Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party joined hands ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, announcing plans to contest all 403 seats under the Samajik Parivartan Morcha banner, with Azad as the alliance's chief ministerial candidate.

n_highlight.h_title: AIMIM and Azad Samaj Party form 'Samajik Parivartan Morcha' to contest UP polls
Alliance plans to contest all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh
Chandrashekhar Azad announced as chief ministerial face of the alliance

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
A new political front has taken shape in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, with Asaduddin Owaisi's All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) and Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) joining hands to form an alliance.

The two parties have formed an alliance named 'Samajik Parivartan Morcha' and announced plans to contest all 403 Assembly seats in the state, with Chandrashekhar Azad as their chief ministerial face.

Announcing the alliance at a joint press conference in Lucknow on Thursday, Owaisi said the new front would seek to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third consecutive term.

#WATCH | Uttar Pradesh | Azad Samaj Party-Kanshiram President and MP, Chandrashekhar Azad and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi announce 'Samajik Parivartan Morcha' for UP polls Azad Samaj Party-Kanshiram President Chandrashekhar Azad says, "This is not a 'Third Front', but a front for social change. It is strong, and it will grow even stronger. As more people from the marginalized, deprived, oppressed, exploited, and downtrodden sections join, this front will become an even more formidable force for those who are oppressed, helpless, and exploited....They promised to eradicate our poverty and helplessness, and to put an end to the oppression, caste-based violence, and atrocities inflicted upon us. But it turned out to be a deception—those who spoke of uplifting us, of bringing us into the mainstream, went on to become MLAs, MPs, Chief Ministers, and even Prime Ministers. Yet, this marginalised community remains exactly where it has always been. The truth is that governments kept changing, announcements kept being made, and even today, the Bahujan community remains deprived of basic amenities..."

— ANI (@ANI) November 12, 2026

The AIMIM chief described the alliance as a strong political alternative and said it would focus on issues concerning Dalits, minorities, backward communities and other marginalised sections.

"I can say with confidence that this will be a strong alternative in Uttar Pradesh to stop the BJP from coming to power for the third time," Owaisi said.

He announced Azad as the alliance's chief ministerial face, saying, "I am happy to announce that our brother Chandrashekhar Aazad will be the chief president of the SPM and its chief ministerial candidate in Uttar Pradesh."

Owaisi also accused political parties of treating backward and Dalit communities, along with other oppressed sections, merely as vote banks.

He said the morcha would raise issues such as the deteriorating condition of education, unemployment among the state's youth and the problems faced by farmers.

"We will do politics for the future. We hope the people of Uttar Pradesh will join hands with Chandrashekhar Aazad to build a better future," he said, adding that the success of the alliance would mean the success of the people of the state.

Responding to suggestions that the SPM was being positioned as a third political front in Uttar Pradesh, Azad said it was not merely another electoral alternative but a platform for social change.

Owaisi also invited people to attend a public meeting scheduled for November 26, describing it as the beginning of a movement for social change in the state.

WHY THE ALLIANCE MATTERS

The formation of the SPM comes as political parties step up preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections, with the BJP seeking a third consecutive term and the Samajwadi Party (SP)-Congress combine looking to challenge its dominance.

The alliance brings together two leaders seeking to consolidate support among Dalits and Muslims, two significant electoral constituencies in Uttar Pradesh.

For Owaisi, the tie-up offers an opportunity to expand AIMIM's political footprint beyond its existing minority support base.

For Azad, it could provide a wider platform to strengthen his party's outreach among Dalit voters, particularly the youth.

The move also comes after Owaisi's attempts to become part of the opposition INDIA bloc's electoral arrangement in Uttar Pradesh failed to make headway.

His offer to participate in seat-sharing discussions with the SP and Congress did not receive a favourable response.

Owaisi had earlier set an October 2 deadline for the two parties to respond to his proposal. With no agreement emerging, AIMIM explored an alternative arrangement with Azad's party.

However, the challenge for the new alliance will be to translate its appeal among Dalit and Muslim voters into electoral gains and establish itself as a viable force in a state where political competition has largely revolved around the BJP and the SP.

HOW THE ALLIANCE COULD AFFECT UP POLITICS

The SPM's entry adds another player to an already competitive electoral landscape, with the BJP-led NDA and the SP-Congress combine expected to be the principal contenders.

In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP won 255 seats, while the SP secured 111. The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) was reduced to just one seat, while the Congress managed to win two.

AIMIM had contested 95 seats in the 2022 elections but failed to win any, securing around 0.49 per cent of the vote. The Azad Samaj Party, too, failed to open its account.

The BSP remains another significant factor in the state's electoral calculations. Party chief Mayawati has indicated that her party will contest the 2027 elections independently, seeking to rebuild its support base among Dalit voters.

news.n_title: Jensen Huang was caught on camera getting cosy with Nvidia VP. Then came the NDA
news.n_description: A bystander filmed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang getting affectionate with company executive Kimberly Powell, adding another explosive twist to the growing controversy surrounding the tech billionaire. The latest revelation comes as Huang faces mounting scrutiny following his admission of an affair with Chinese businesswoman, whom US intelligence suspect of being a spy.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
A bystander who recorded Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and senior company executive Kimberly Powell being affectionate at a California hotel during the chipmaker's annual developer conference in March was confronted by the billionaire's private security personnel and asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA), according to a New York Times report.

The incident took place in San Jose, where Nvidia was hosting its annual GTC conference that brings together developers, researchers, business leaders, and engineers.

While Huang and other company executives were holding meetings at a hotel nearby, the Nvidia CEO and Powell, who is also married, were seen displaying affection, the newspaper reported, citing sources.

One person at the hotel captured the interaction on a mobile phone. Huang's security personnel noticed the recording and took the bystander aside, the sources told The New York Times.

The security workers then asked the person to sign the NDA barring them from disclosing what they had witnessed.

The episode adds another dimension to the scrutiny surrounding the billionaire's admission of his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy by American intelligence.

Powell, 48, has been with Nvidia since 2008 and currently serves as its vice president of healthcare.

Powell also featured at the March conference, where she spoke about the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate advances in healthcare and biology.

Her presentation included cartoon illustrations of Jensen Huang.

Powell's career at Nvidia has spanned more than 18 years. She initially worked on expanding the use of the company's AI chips in medical imaging, was promoted to senior director in 2016 and became vice president of healthcare by late 2017, according to her professional profile and LinkedIn page.

Her current responsibilities cover Nvidia's healthcare hardware and software business, including technologies used in medical imaging, life sciences and drug discovery.

Jensen Huang, Powell and Nvidia declined to comment on the matter, the report said.

In the wake of the controversies, the 63-year-old tech giant's position is currently under scrutiny. According to a Wall Street Journal report, the company's board is planning to remove him and name a new CEO.

Since Jensen Huang sent an e-mail to company employees confessing to his affair with Alice Huang on November 8, Nvidia has lost nearly $600 billion in market value.

news.n_title: No bank account? You can still send up to Rs 50,000 through a bank branch
news.n_description: The RBI has consolidated existing rules for Domestic Money Transfers, clarifying how much customers can send through bank branches, ATMs and business correspondents, and how much recipients without bank accounts can collect in cash.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
You don't have a bank account but need to send money to someone who does? You can still walk into a bank branch, deposit cash and transfer up to Rs 50,000 directly into the beneficiary's account.

This facility is not new. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) framework to make small-value fund transfers easier through formal banking channels, particularly for people such as migrant workers who may not have easy access to banking services.

The central bank has now consolidated and harmonised its existing instructions through the Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026, which came into effect on November 11.

The directions spell out the limits applicable to different types of domestic money transfers, including cash deposits at bank branches, transfers through ATMs and Business Correspondents, and cash payouts to recipients who do not have bank accounts.

Here is what the clarified rules mean for customers.

HOW MUCH CAN YOU SEND WITHOUT A BANK ACCOUNT?

Under the directions, a walk-in customer at a bank branch can deposit cash and remit up to Rs 50,000 directly into a beneficiary's bank account through the National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) system.

This means you do not necessarily need to hold a bank account to use this facility. You can visit a bank branch and use its cash pay-in service to transfer money to someone who has a bank account.

The facility can be particularly useful for people who need to send money to family members in other cities or states but do not have access to conventional banking services themselves.

WHAT IF YOU USE AN ATM OR BUSINESS CORRESPONDENT?

The limits are lower if you use an ATM or a Business Correspondent (BC) to transfer money.

Under the RBI's directions, you can transfer up to Rs 5,000 per transaction. The total amount transferred cannot exceed Rs 25,000 per remitter in a month.

Business Correspondents are agents authorised by banks to provide basic banking services, including cash deposits and withdrawals, particularly in areas where customers may not have easy access to a bank branch.

So, if you regularly send money through a BC or an ATM, remember that the Rs 5,000 limit applies to each transaction, while Rs 25,000 is the overall monthly cap for the remitter.

CAN SOMEONE WITHOUT A BANK ACCOUNT RECEIVE MONEY?

Yes. The RBI has also clarified the rules for what it calls the Cash Pay-out Service.

Under this facility, a person with a bank account can transfer money from their account for delivery in cash to a recipient who does not have a bank account.

The recipient can collect the money through an ATM, a Business Correspondent or another authorised payment channel.

However, the RBI has set limits. A maximum of Rs 10,000 can be transferred for cash payment in a single transaction. The total amount cannot exceed Rs 25,000 per beneficiary in a month.

For example, if you are sending money to a family member who does not have a bank account, the recipient can collect up to Rs 10,000 in cash in a single transaction, subject to the overall monthly ceiling of Rs 25,000.

WHY HAS THE RBI ISSUED FRESH DIRECTIONS?

The Domestic Money Transfer framework was originally introduced to facilitate small-value transfers through formal banking channels.

It is particularly relevant for people, including migrant workers, who may need to send money home but face difficulties accessing conventional banking services because of a lack of identity or address documentation.

The latest directions are aimed at bringing the existing instructions together and harmonising the rules governing different types of domestic money transfers. They also clarify the limits and safeguards that banks and non-bank entities must follow.

In other words, the RBI has not announced a new money-transfer facility. It has consolidated the existing framework and set out the applicable rules in a single set of directions.

WHAT SAFEGUARDS MUST BANKS FOLLOW?

The RBI has also stressed the need for stronger monitoring to prevent misuse of these facilities.

Banks and non-bank entities must put in place safeguards such as transaction velocity checks and alerts to customers when money is credited into accounts through these facilities.

If there is an unusual increase in the volume of credits into a particular account or a group of accounts, the institution must investigate it immediately.

Suspicious transactions must also be reported to the appropriate authorities.

The RBI has said that transfers under the facility are expected to take place in real time or near real time, allowing beneficiaries to receive money without long delays.

One important exclusion is that card-to-card transfers do not fall under the scope of the new directions.

news.n_title: PM Modi to address over 2,000 farmers at Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference tonight
news.n_description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 tonight. The summit connects farmers with policymakers, industry leaders and experts shaping agriculture's future.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will deliver the plenary address at the India Today Group's Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 tonight. The two-day event will bring together over 2,000 farmers, policymakers, industry leaders and global experts at Bharat Mandapam.

The Prime Minister is scheduled to speak at 8 pm. His address will be simulcast on all the three market-leading broadcast channels, all 30 YouTube channels, all the five leading news websites and social media platforms (that command a 50 per cent market dominance) of the India Today Group.

Participation is by invitation/pre-registration only. For a hassle-free entry, registered invitees must reach the venue not later than 4 pm carrying their Aadhaar card for identification.

The two-day international conference, organised by the India Today Group, began on Wednesday and is being held under the theme 'Smart Kisan, Viksit Bharat'. The event is being presented by Mahindra Tractors and co-presented by Mahadhan Agritech.

The Prime Minister's address will take place in the Plenary Hall of Bharat Mandapam, which has a seating capacity of 2,700. The engagement is expected to bring farmers from across the country into direct conversation with the national leadership and experts working on the future of agriculture.

The conference aims to examine the next phase of growth in Indian agriculture, with discussions focusing on emerging technologies, sustainability, climate resilience and opportunities for farmers. Key areas of discussion include precision farming, artificial intelligence-driven resource management and climate-resilient crop varieties.

The first day of the conference saw participation from Union Minister Chirag Paswan, Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, among other speakers.

On Thursday, Delhi MP Manoj Tiwari is among the speakers scheduled to participate, alongside other policymakers and experts.

Announcing the conference, Aroon Purie, Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of the India Today Group said, "Agriculture is India’s biggest profession, and its future dictates our nation's destiny. We are deeply honoured that PM Modi will deliver the plenary address at the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026. Through this summit, we are bringing the ingenuity of our farmers into direct dialogue with global science, policy, and industry to engineer lasting, tech-enabled prosperity."

Kalli Purie, Vice Chairperson and Executive Editor-in-Chief of the India Today Group, said, "India's most compelling narratives of grit and innovation originate in our villages. With the Prime Minister addressing the concluding session, this platform gives those grassroots voices the ultimate national and global resonance, reinforcing our core belief that an empowered 'Smart Kisan' is the beating heart of a Viksit Bharat."

The conference seeks to place farmers and their aspirations at the centre of discussions on India's agricultural transformation, while exploring how innovation, technology and policy can contribute to the vision of a developed India.

news.n_title: Delay in Army action: Sonia Gandhi's 1984 riots claim was busted 40 years ago
news.n_description: During the 1984 anti-Sikh pogrom, had the Army been deployed sooner in Delhi, at least 2,000 lives could have been saved. Congress leader Sonia Gandhi writes the delay was due to then Army Chief Gen AS Vaidya's decision. However, the deposition of Gen Vaidya and the Misra Commission findings busted those claims 40 years ago.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
"Many contradictory reports have appeared about that harrowing period, some concerning the delay in the deployment of the army," writes Congress leader Sonia Gandhi in her memoir on the 1984 anti-Sikh pogrom that followed the assassination of the prime minister and her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi. The pogrom, in which over 2,700 Sikhs were killed in Delhi alone, is one of the darkest chapters in modern Indian history and blamed on Congress leaders.

Among several issues, Sonia Gandhi's account of the 1984 anti-Sikh pogrom in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, released on Tuesday (November 10), has sparked an intense debate.

Sonia Gandhi says the Army was ordered to be deployed on October 31, 1984, the very day when Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards, but the delay was on part of the military brass.

In his submission to the Justice Ranganath Misra Commission that was set up in 1985 to inquire into the 1984 riots, Army Chief General AS Vaidya said soldiers had been deployed on October 31 itself but never utilised.

The delay, as the Misra Commission would hear, was due to Delhi's Lieutenant Governor and the Police Commissioner, who insisted on going around and taking stock of the ground situation before soldiers could be deployed.

The Misra Commission found that had the around 5,000 soldiers present in Delhi been pressed into service, the lives of at least 2,000 Sikhs could have been saved.

Several people have now countered Sonia Gandhi's accounts of the 1984 massacre in her memoir, questioning her version of the timeline.

HS Phoolka, a Senior Advocate who fought for the 1984 victims and is now a BJP member, said her claims were "absolutely false".

Columnist and author Tavleen Singh said Sonia Gandhi's memoir was "fascinating", but "the whitewashing of the Congress role in the 1984 pogrom is unforgivable".

Let us have a look at the timeline of Indira Gandhi's assassination and the days of the rioting and killing to put the debate in context.

TIMELINE OF INDIRA GANDHI'S ASSASSINATION AND ANTI-SIKH POGROM OF 1984

June 1–8, 1984: Then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi ordered the Army to storm the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar as part of Operation Blue Star to remove Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale-led Sikh insurgents.

October 31, 1984: Indira Gandhi shot by her bodyguards around 9.30 am. Rushed to AIIMS, where doctors pronounced her dead at approximately 2:20 pm.

October 31, 1984: Initial unrest begins with crowds outside AIIMS targeting the motorcade of President Zail Singh at around 5.30 pm. Rajiv Gandhi sworn in as PM, Indira's death announced on Doordarshan. Late-night attacks on Sikhs

November 1, 1984: Organised attacks on Sikh-majority neighborhoods across Delhi, including Trilokpuri, Sultanpuri, and Mangolpuri

November 2, 1984: Large-scale killings continues unchecked in outer Delhi colonies. Curfew declared in Delhi, and Army deployment announced in the afternoon.

November 3, 1984: Army receives shoot-at-sight orders and starts patrolling Delhi streets. Indira Gandhi cremated in the afternoon

WHAT SONIA GANDHI WRITES ABOUT 1984 RIOTS IN MEMOIR

In Chapter 17 (Page 265) of her memoir, Sonia Gandhi writes that Army deployment was ordered on October 31 itself but General Vaidya didn't prefer the mobilisation of some nearby units.

"Although the Chief of Army Staff, General AS Vaidya, had received his orders the same night as the assassination, we heard later that he decided not to mobilise the nearest units because they were manned by Sikh soldiers, a factor that might have exacerbated the situation," writes Sonia in Belonging.

"Following Operation Blue Star, there had been sporadic mutinies in Gurdaspur, Ramgarh in Bihar, Pune, and Jammu by Sikh soldiers, in which a number of Sikh officers had also participated," she explains.

"Whatever the reason, General Vaidya ordered units further away, in Dehradun, to move to Delhi. This took some time, but by the night of November 1, army units had started moving into place and by noon of November 2 had been positioned in parts of the city affected by rioting; a curfew was in force and shoot-at-sight orders had been issued," writes Sonia.

"Meanwhile, civil society had also helped with setting up relief camps around the city to protect and feed the traumatised survivors. Order was finally restored, and the rioting came to an end."

WHAT GENERAL VAIDYA SAID ABOUT ARMY DEPLOYMENT IN DELHI IN 1984

General Vaidya's remarks are captured in the Misra Commission report, and not the Nanavati Commission (2000-2005) report.

General Vaidya was assassinated in Pune by Khalistanis on August 10, 1986. He didn't live to see the final report. The Misra Commission report was submitted in August 1986, but tabled in Parliament only in February 1987.

General Vaidya told the Misra Commission that by about 10.30 am on October 31, 1984, he had directed a Brigade from Meerut to be moved to Delhi and this Brigade had reached Delhi before midnight. This Brigade had 1,600 fighting officers and jawans.

At Delhi, the usual Army strength was somewhere between 5,500 and 6,000 strong.

Major General JS Jamwal, GOC Delhi Area, was ordered to provide all assistance, and told the Commission that he had 6,100 soldiers with him in Delhi, 3,000 for field duty and 3,100 who were being used for controlling movements at Teenmurti Bhavan where Indira's body was lying in state, and at Shakti Sthal where she was to be cremated.

By the time the brigade directed by General Vaidya to reach Delhi arrived on the night of October 31, the number of troops ready to be mobilised had risen to 5,000. This number included two infantry brigades, two artillery regiments, an engineering regiments, and personnel at the Rajputana Rifles Training Centre.

All that was needed was the go-ahead from Delhi's civil authorities.

WHO DID MISRA COMMISSION BLAME FOR THE KILLING OF SIKHS IN 1984?

The Misra Commission found the statement of Police Commissioner Subhash Tandon that adequate Army personnel were not available in Delhi to be without basis.

Lt Governor PG Gavai stated to the Commission that in the early morning of November 1, he was apprehensive that the situation might worsen and "had advised the Commissioner of Police that the Army may be called".

The Commission also noted that Gautam Kaul, Additional Commissioner of Police, had warned Tandon that the Delhi Police "were not in a position to match the challenging task that followed the assassination of Indira Gandhi."

"It is at that point of time that the Commissioner of Police wanted a personal assessment to be made of the situation by moving around. This took quite some time," according to the Commission's report.

The Misra Commission blamed the delay in Army deployment squarely on Lt Governor Gavai and the Commissioner of Police. Both were under the Congress-led Union government. And both were the only ones who could request the Indian Army's assistance to curb the violence.

There have been eyewitness accounts stating that Congress leaders, including Jagdish Tytler and Sajjan Kumar, directing mobs to attack Sikh families.

Tandon was removed as the Commissioner of Police in November 1984.

"If the Army had been called in on the morning of November 1, 1984 — and by then about 5,000 Army people were at Delhi — the position would certainly not have been as bad as it turned out to be. 5,000 Army jawans divided into columns and moving into. the streets properly armed would not have brought about the death of at least 2,000 people," the Commission concluded regarding Army deployment.

THE REACTION TO SONIA GANDHI'S 1984 ARMY CLAIMS

The Ahuja Committee, set up in 1987, put the all-India death toll in the anti-Sikh pogrom of 1984 at 3,325, of whom 2,733 Sikhs were killed in Delhi.

Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi on November 19, reacting to the anti-Sikh pogrom, said: "... When Indira's assassination happened, there were riots in the country. We know that the hearts of the Indian people were full of anger and that for a few days people felt India was shaking. When a big tree falls, the earth shakes."

Timely deployment of Army personnel, who were present in the Capital, could have saved at least 2,000 Sikhs in Delhi, according to the Misra Commission. General Vaidya said he had given the orders, and the Commission said it was the civilian administration that delayed the deployment.

Sonia Gandhi, in her memoir Belonging, says the Army got the order on October 31 itself, and the delay was due to the decision of General Vaidya.

BJP leader HS Phoolka said on Tuesday said the claim was "absolutely false".

"As per the official record by the [Misra] Commission, by the Govt, the Army was called in on the evening of November 1 and the Army arrived only on the evening of November 2. In its report, Misra Commission stated that 5,000 Army personnel were available within Delhi, and they were not deployed," Phoolka told ANI.

He cited the Misra Commission to say that "had they been deployed, lives of 2,000 Sikhs could have been saved."

Shiromani Akali Dal chief and former Punjab Deputy Chief Minister Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked Punjab Congress leaders, saying they "must break their criminal silence on the clean chit given by Sonia Gandhi to the killers of thousands of innocent Sikhs in 1984".

"Her admission that Rajiv Gandhi purposely and personally decided not to deploy Army units in Delhi because they included Sikh personnel finally provides the clinching evidence of Congress govt patronage of the anti-Sikh massacre," Badal wrote on X.

The 1984 anti-Sikh pogrom is one of the darkest chapters of modern Indian history. Sonia Gandhi might have tried to secure a clean chit for Rajiv Gandhi, but Badal is now using her arguments to attack her. The issue of Army deployment was made clear with the tabling of the Misra Commission report in 1987 itself.

news.n_title: Woman confronts molester on Mumbai local, gets pushed under moving train, loses arm
news.n_description: A 20-year-old woman lost her left arm and sustained head injury after being pushed onto the tracks at Maharashtra's Naigaon station for confronting a man over a molestation attempt aboard a local train.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
A 20-year-old woman lost her left arm after she was molested and pushed onto the tracks during a local train journey by a man at Maharashtra's Naigaon railway station on November 4.

The incident occurred when the woman was returning home to Naigaon East from Borivali last week after visiting her sister in Goregaon.

According to police, an unidentified passenger tried to molest a woman around 7.15 pm, following which she confronted him and demanded an explanation after getting off at Naigaon railway station.

A heated argument followed, during which she threw her slipper at the man, who retaliated by hurling his slipper at her before shoving her forcefully towards the tracks.

She fell through the gap between two railway coaches just as the local train began moving, leaving her unable to climb back onto the platform.

Her left arm was run over by the train and severed near the elbow, police said, adding that she was undergoing treatment at a hospital.

The woman also sustained head injuries and required 16 stitches.

Police examined CCTV footage from multiple locations to identify the accused and arrested him on November 9, Senior Police Inspector Ganpat Tumbada said.

news.n_title: Chinese vloggers pass off Dhaka slums as New Delhi's, then vanish into thin air
news.n_description: Chinese vloggers who portrayed Bangladesh's slums as those in New Delhi have stopped appearing in the Dhaka neighbourhood following media reports and increased police surveillance. The controversy drew a sharp reaction from India.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Scores of Chinese nationals who had descended on Dhaka's streets, filming the Bangladeshi capital's impoverished working-class neighbourhoods and passing off the footage as scenes from New Delhi have disappeared from the area overnight, following media reports that exposed their activities and increased police surveillance. India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) also recently flagged their activities as "peddling of false narratives", while seeking action against them from Bangladeshi authorities.

A fresh report by Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo on Wednesday (November 11) said the Chinese nationals who had been livestreaming from Uttara's Sector 12 and adjoining Tekpara were no longer visible in the neighbourhood. The newspaper said its correspondents visited the areas, but did not spot any Chinese nationals filming.

India Today Digital had reported on the controversy on November 9, following reports by Bangladeshi outlets, including Prothom Alo, The Business Standard and Kaler Kantho.

The recent report suggested that the Chinese vloggers had stopped appearing in the neighbourhood from November 7. This was a day after the Dhaka-based Prothom Alo published its investigation, documenting the activities of more than 150 Chinese nationals.

Locals too said the vloggers had disappeared.

"This bridge was the Chinese people's base. They would make videos here all day and night. They would film us and the passengers too. I haven't seen them for some time now. I don't know if something has happened," a rickshaw puller, Imam ul Islam, told Prothom Alo.

Another resident, Mohammad Selim, said he had earlier seen several Chinese men and women visiting the neighbourhood every day to film videos.

The disappearance came amid increased scrutiny by Bangladeshi authorities following the media reports. Police and intelligence personnel began monitoring the Chinese nationals, checking their visas and passports and questioning why they were undertaking such activities on tourist visas.

Mohammad Khalid Mansur, officer-in-charge of Uttara West police station, told Prothom Alo that the activities had declined following the increased surveillance.

"Due to the activities of law enforcement agencies, such activities by Chinese nationals have decreased. Police and intelligence personnel are monitoring them. Their activities are being observed through various agencies," he said.

INDIA'S MEA FLAGS MISLEADING VIDEOS BY CHINESE VLOGGERS

The India Today Digital report on November 9 highlighted how Chinese nationals were livestreaming from Dhaka's low-income neighbourhoods while claiming to be broadcasting from India's capital and making disparaging remarks about Indian living conditions.

The controversy also drew a response from New Delhi. On November 10, a day after the India Today Digital report, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, during his fortnightly press conference, said the Indian government had taken note of the Bangladeshi media reports and called for appropriate action against those involved.

Responding to a question at the MEA's weekly briefing, Jaiswal said, "It is unfortunate that people are using the territory of one country to malign another country."

He added that those involved in creating and propagating false narratives should understand that such activities also damage their own country's credibility.

"Those who are involved in this and those behind this are both culpable," Jaiswal said, adding that appropriate action should be taken against them.

#WATCH | Delhi: On Chinese vloggers reportedly livestreaming from slums in Dhaka, MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal says, "We have seen media reports in this regard. Such efforts to present a distorted picture of any country are unfortunate. Insofar as efforts to buy foreign elements to portray Dhaka as Delhi are concerned, the peddling of false narratives only undermines the credibility of those who are undertaking such actions and those who are behind them. And I would urge the authorities concerned to take action against such people."

— ANI (@ANI) November 10, 2026

WHAT WERE THE CHINESE VLOGGERS DOING IN DHAKA?

The Chinese nationals had reportedly been filming in Dhaka's Uttara for several months, focusing on narrow lanes, residential areas, local shops and the homes of impoverished residents. Their footage was livestreamed on Chinese social media platforms, including WeChat and Douyin.

In its November 6 investigation, Prothom Alo identified a Chinese woman called Mianmian, who introduced Uttara's Sector 12 as New Delhi while describing its homes as dirty, underdeveloped and unhygienic.

Another Chinese national, identified as Wang Wei, was seen filming at tea stalls in Tekpara. He told viewers that locals were drinking tea made from "cow urine" and "dirty river water".

The purpose of the activity, however, remains unclear. Prothom Alo reported that some Bangladeshis were being paid to assist the vloggers. One Chinese national, identified as Fangyou, reportedly told the newspaper that the livestreams were part of product-promotion activities but declined to explain why the neighbourhoods had been selected.

An earlier report by The Business Standard in May had also documented Chinese vloggers filming in Dhaka's low-income settlements, with videos often carrying descriptions such as "poor", "dirty" and "slum".

Neither the Bangladeshi investigations nor the subsequent reporting established whether the vloggers were operating independently or as part of an organised campaign.

Western fascination with poverty in South Asia, particularly in India, is very well known. But the repackaging of footage from Dhaka's poorest neighbourhoods as being from India by Chinese vloggers raises questions. Are they trying to cash in on a social media trend or is it part of a coordinated disinformation campaign targeting India?

There's a fresh question now. Are these Chinese vloggers gone for good, or whether they have simply beaten a temporary retreat?

news.n_title: When Jensen Huang met Alice, her Chinese husband played matchmaker
news.n_description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was introduced to Alice Huang by her husband, Kang Wei, who reportedly knew about their relationship and even joked about their closeness. The couple built a business empire spanning technology and cloud computing, but their links to Huang and alleged exports of restricted Nvidia AI chips to China have triggered investigations.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was introduced to Alice Huang, who later became his romantic interest, by her husband, Chinese businessman Kang Wei, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people who know the couple.

Kang, who had known Jensen Huang for about a decade, had reportedly accepted their relationship for two years and openly discussed their closeness. He sometimes joked to associates that his wife was Jensen Huang's personal assistant. However, the report does not specify when Kang introduced Alice to Jensen Huang.

Now, Kang's relationship with Jensen Huang has come under scrutiny as authorities examine the couple's business activities and their links to the Nvidia chief.

US officials believe Chinese intelligence services recruited Alice Huang as an asset because of her access to Jensen Huang, while Nvidia's board is preparing to remove him as chief executive after another alleged affair emerged on Wednesday.

In a letter to employees on Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted being unfaithful to his wife and apologised for breaching the trust of his family and staff.

Kang and Alice Huang used their personal connections while pursuing business opportunities in China, Singapore, Taiwan and other markets, The Wall Street Journal further reported, citing people familiar with their dealings.

Over the past decade, they moved from one venture to another, involving video game companies, pharmaceutical takeovers and cloud computing.

They established related entities, transferred holdings between themselves and drew on their contacts to pursue business opportunities.

Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips became their latest business focus after years of pursuing fast-growing investment opportunities and occasionally running into regulatory trouble.

The couple is now facing several investigations, with scrutiny widening over their relationship with Jensen Huang.

ALICE HUANG'S COMPANY UNDER US SCANNER

Authorities in the US and Singapore are examining Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud services provider, over allegations that it may have transshipped billions of dollars' worth of export-restricted Nvidia AI chips to China.

People familiar with the matter told The Wall Street Journal that Megaspeed sent some Nvidia-powered servers to China, potentially bypassing US restrictions on such exports.

Taiwanese authorities have revoked Alice Huang's entry permit and barred her from returning to the island, where she met Jensen Huang several times.

Officials in Taiwan said they were investigating whether her visits involved intelligence gathering or breached the island's anti-infiltration law.

Singapore authorities detained Alice Huang in the summer of 2025 and prevented her from leaving the country, according to people briefed on the detention, The Wall Street Journal reported. The travel restriction was later lifted, and she was in China earlier this year, they said.

Singapore's government has said its investigation into Megaspeed is continuing but that it has not examined Alice Huang's links to China. It did not respond to questions about her detention.

Kang was detained in Shanghai earlier this year in connection with inquiries into alleged stock market manipulation involving listed companies. He was recently released and later shared a photograph of himself with friends at Stanford University, according to people who know the couple.

HOW ALICE, HER HUSBAND BUILT THEIR BUSINESS EMPIRE

Kang, now in his early 50s, was previously a prominent fund manager in China before establishing Shanghai Hexi in 2010. Alice Huang, who is in her late 40s, pursued a master's degree in media management at Hong Kong Baptist University in the late 2000s, according to another graduate of the programme.

It could not be established when the couple met, but Shanghai Hexi, whose name translates as "harmonious prosperity", became central to their business partnership. Corporate registry records show that they began jointly running the company in 2016.

Shanghai Hexi invested in several technology businesses, including video game companies. Those investments gave Kang an opportunity to meet Jensen Huang in the 2010s, when the latter was an emerging Silicon Valley chief executive. Nvidia primarily made chips for video games at the time. A person who worked at one of Kang's portfolio companies said he helped arrange a meeting between the two men in Asia.

China's securities regulator fined Kang and Shanghai Hexi in 2018 for failing to disclose their holdings in a Chinese pharmaceutical company and for other violations linked to a takeover battle. Kang and the company challenged the findings at official hearings, but the regulator rejected their arguments.

By the early 2020s, Kang and Alice Huang had shifted their attention to cloud computing, which provides remote computing capacity to corporate customers. Through a company partly owned by a fund they managed, they began developing relationships with some of China's major technology groups.

In 2023, the couple moved into AI data centres. Corporate filings and people familiar with the matter said they acquired the Singapore division of a video game company in which they had previously invested. The unit was renamed Megaspeed International in March 2023, with Alice Huang registered as a director. Kang worked alongside her to develop the company, the people said.

HOW MEGASPEED GAINED ACCESS TO NVIDIA AI CHIPS

Alibaba, the Chinese e-commerce company that has also expanded into AI, played an important role in Megaspeed's launch, according to people familiar with negotiations at the time.

The US had begun imposing export restrictions on advanced chips in late 2022, preventing Nvidia from selling them directly to China over concerns that they could strengthen the country's military and surveillance capabilities.

Alibaba was seeking a partner that could provide access to computing capacity from data centres outside China equipped with Nvidia chips, the people said. Megaspeed told Nvidia that Alibaba would be its anchor customer, offering enough business to help the company secure priority access to chips as an Nvidia cloud partner in November 2023.

Soon afterwards, Alice Huang told an associate that she had contacted Jensen Huang and that Megaspeed's operations would begin smoothly.

The company installed many of the Nvidia servers it acquired at data centres in Malaysia and supplied computing capacity to Alibaba, according to people familiar with the matter.

Megaspeed also shipped some servers to China, including to Century Litong, a Shanghai-based cloud computing provider owned by a Shanghai-listed company that had previously conducted business with Kang, the people said.

US rules prohibited the export of advanced Nvidia AI chips to China at the time and continue to do so. The Information had previously reported the connection between Megaspeed and Century Litong.

Megaspeed has said that it operates "fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations" and upholds the highest standards of lawful conduct. Century Litong did not respond to a request for comment.

Kang and Alice Huang subsequently sought to expand their operations. Investors approached by the couple in Shanghai and Singapore said they presented several data centre proposals between late 2024 and June 2025, including two projects in Southeast Asia and one in Shanghai.

The prospective investors said the couple claimed that investments could triple in value within three years and expressed confidence that they had ways to bring Nvidia chips into China.

Photographs and accounts from people who encountered them show that Alice Huang met Jensen Huang repeatedly during the same period between 2024 and 2025. At a dinner in Taiwan in May 2025, local media captured Jensen Huang's daughter cheerfully taking photographs of the pair.

news.n_title: Alice's wish was Jensen's command? Here's what went down at a Taipei party
news.n_description: Alice Huang openly flaunted her access to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a Taipei party in June 2024, telling a group of tech executives she could bring him there, according to a New York Times report.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
A little after midnight at a tech party in Taipei in June 2024, Alice Huang, a businesswoman who has come into focus over suspected links to Chinese espionage and an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, made a bold claim before a group of technology executives. She said she could get the billionaire to join them. Moments later, Jensen Huang walked in.

"I bet you guys I can get Jensen here," Alice Huang told the group, according to Parker Schmitt, who is chief executive of NetThunder, a data software provider, who witnessed the exchange and later recounted it to The New York Times.

Jensen Huang arrived with two other Nvidia executives and joined the group for a shot of whiskey. However, a person familiar with Nvidia told the media house that the CEO had already planned to attend the gathering.

The exchange offered a glimpse into the access Alice Huang appeared to enjoy with one of the most influential figures in the technology industry.

According to Schmitt, Alice was keen to establish herself as a successful sales executive and her association with Jensen Huang helped build her professional image.

Her social media profiles were filled with photographs of the two together, including pictures taken at a golf course and restaurants where they shared wine. "Photos with Jensen are a point of pride," Schmitt said.

Reports that US authorities were investigating Alice Huang over suspected links to Chinese intelligence first surfaced in October, with officials believing she was gathering information for Beijing as part of a foreign intelligence operation.

Her association with Singapore-based data centre company, Megaspeed, added another dimension to the allegations.

The company purchased more than USD 4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over two years, raising questions about their eventual destination amid US restrictions on exports of advanced semiconductor technology to China.

According to the NYT report, US President Donald Trump had been briefed about the intelligence allegations roughly a year before they became public. Jensen Huang, however, was never formally warned that he could be a target of a foreign intelligence operation.

Nvidia had previously defended its dealings with Megaspeed, with Jensen Huang describing the business relationship as normal. The company said it had examined the deployment of its graphics processing units (GPUs) and checked that its chips had not been illegally diverted to China.

The controversy erupted after Jensen Huang broke his silence and admitted in an email to Nvidia employees that he was unfaithful to his wife, Lori Huang, and apologised to her and their children for his actions.

"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and her children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," the 63-year-old said.

He also acknowledged failing in his responsibilities towards Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders, and vowed to regain their trust.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's board has launched an independent inquiry, to be conducted by a committee of independent directors with the assistance of external legal counsel. Huang has backed the probe and pledged full cooperation.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the company said, stressing its commitment to US national and economic security.

The chipmaker's board meets today to decide whether to remove him.

The allegations have also drawn congressional attention. Three Republican committee chairmen, namely Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, wrote to Huang on November 4 seeking a closed-door briefing on potential national security risks, China's access to sensitive US technology and Nvidia's safeguards against foreign intelligence operations.

They asked him to appear on November 18.

Nvidia has maintained that Huang interacts with thousands of customer executives every year and that its cloud customers in Asia have access only to ordinary business information, not sensitive trade secrets or US national security-related information.

The controversy comes at a critical time for Nvidia, whose chips power AI infrastructure used by technology giants such as OpenAI and Meta. Co-founded by Huang in 1993, the company evolved from a graphics processing firm largely associated with gaming into a semiconductor powerhouse at the heart of the AI boom.

However, its estimated USD 4.5 trillion valuation has come under pressure amid concerns over the sustainability of AI spending and a broader technology sell-off. Its shares have also erased their gains for the year.

news.n_title: From the India Today archives (2011) | Cancer or conjecture? Sonia Gandhi's secret battle
news.n_description: INDIA TODAY's 2011 report on Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's cancer treatment that she has now detailed in her autobiography 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
(NOTE: This article was originally published in the India Today issue dated October 10, 2011)

The news is good. The operation was a success. She is back in India and has begun to defuse the life-threatening crisis within Congress and government at a time when what she really needs is some rest. India doesn’t know what exactly ails its most powerful citizen. The one unanswered question, which continues to fuel speculation ranging from the ignorant to the bizarre, is: why did the authorities keep details of Sonia Gandhi’s medical condition such a tightly wrapped secret?

Some word has begun to trickle down since Sonia has returned. She has confided to a select few Congress leaders that she had first stage cancer, for which she went through a seven-hour-long surgical procedure. "In June, when Congressmen claimed that she had gone abroad to tend to her ailing mother, she had gone for her own treatment," a Congress leader told INDIA TODAY. "The good news is that the illness is not life-threatening. However, it will be at least six months before she will be able to handle the normal workload," the source said.

India has substituted news with plenty of conjecture. Since August 4, when BBC and Agence France-Presse broke the news of Sonia Gandhi’s surgery, Delhi’s politically connected physicians have been in demand. Some have been toeing the Congress line that it’s a private matter, some reprimanding nosy reporters, some citing the Hippocratic Oath while most are denying any knowledge. Various theories have been doing the rounds in a season of enforced silence-that it could be gastrointestinal or gynaecological cancer.

At the centre of all this is the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center in New York, US, where Sonia reportedly had her surgery. According to some doctors, speaking in strict confidentiality, the seven-hour-long surgery indicates a rare and difficult cancer. They said the 64-year-old Congress president was initially diagnosed with an "unspecified mass" in her pancreas. The tests indicated the probability of the rare neuroendocrine tumour of the pancreas (pNET).

The more common pancreatic cancers, adenocarcinoma, are virulent and have a survival rate of about two per cent. But pNET is more slow-spreading and treatable. "The long OT time could be because pNET is so rare. It affects less than one person in 100,000 in the US," the doctors told INDIA TODAY.

The operation could have taken long, says a doctor who refuses to be identified, because, post-operation, the biopsy revealed that it wasn’t probably a cancer at all. "It was most likely an unusual disorder, pancreatic tuberculosis, which very often mimics pNET," he said. The symptoms for pancreatic tb and cancer can be surprisingly similar, making diagnosis virtually impossible: from fever and fatigue to weight loss to upper abdominal pain radiating to the back.

Radiological imaging techniques, ultrasonography, CT scan and other tests usually fail to make a clear distinction. "It’s a very lucky and extremely rare misdiagnosis but not totally unheard of," says the doctor. At the world’s top cancer facility, a patient with an unspecified mass can get a biopsy, an ultrasound for size and surgical procedure, all in a day. The doctors took time to detect it correctly and put Sonia on heavy-duty anti-tb therapy (reportedly for the next six months). "She should be fine after that," he says.

Beyond pNET and pancreatic tuberculosis is another theory. It stems from her physician of choice in the US. Internationally-known cancer specialist, Dr Dattatreyudu Nori, is professor and executive vice chair of radiation oncology at the New York-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical College in New York City hospital. Nori is an acclaimed expert in women’s cancer. He has been named as one of the top doctors in the US for the treatment of women by one of the most popular women’s magazines, The Ladies Home Journal. Nori was on vacation in Iceland at that time, but was apparently called back urgently and returned to New York to coordinate the entire procedure for Sonia. Nori has neither confirmed nor denied that he was treating her.

There is no final official word on the Congress President’s health but what can be confirmed is that the Congress party seems to have become suicidal. The most obvious manifestation of it is the sight of a hapless prime minister reduced to a bystander while the turf war between two of his senior Cabinet colleagues, Finance Minister Pranab Mukherjee and Home Minister P. Chidambaram, takes a heavy toll on governance.

Sonia remains the absolute authority where all arguments stop. The PM has fallen from grace, while Rahul has failed to rise to the occasion. According to a party official who met Sonia recently, "she is not happy with the handling of the 2G letter conflict by the prime minister." He was referring to a March 25, 2011, note written by the finance ministry to the PMO which stated that Chidambaram could have prevented the 2G scam by insisting on an auction.

Mukherjee is blaming the PMO for giving such a detailed response to an otherwise general RTI inquiry, as well as for demanding such a note in the first place. In a four-page letter written to the Prime Minister, he has said that it was at the behest of the then Cabinet Secretary K.M. Chandrasekhar that such a note was prepared. According to finance ministry sources, the letter states "the finance ministry sent a 12-paragraph note apprising the cabinet secretary of the facts but this was sent back with paragraphs added." Whether he wanted it or not, the Prime Minster has become party to the deepening crisis.

Though Mukherjee rushed to New York on September 25 to meet Manmohan, who was attending the UN General Assembly, and Chidambaram had been in touch with the Prime Minister on the phone, Sonia still had to step in for damage control. On her return home on September 8 from the medical treatment in the US, there was hardly any political news to cheer her up. She has questioned her colleagues about the fallout of the Anna Hazare fiasco. Saddled with a Prime Minister who lacks political authority and a son whose disinterest is only matched by his diffidence, an ailing Sonia does not have the luxury of a quiet recuperation.

There has been speculation ever since she left for treatment that she would appoint Rahul as Congress working president. That has not happened. The main reason for this is Rahul himself. He is not sure of himself, and now it looks like even the party is coming to terms with the reality of a reluctant prince. Soon after the 2G letter crisis broke, Rahul flew to Srinagar where, for two days, he dabbled in Youth Congress matters and breakfasted with his pal, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah. Just as he refused to play an active role during the Anna Hazare agitation he has gone out of his way to distance himself from this crisis too.

The four-member core group that Sonia had appointed to run the party when she left for her treatment on August 4 has already been disbanded. It held no structured meetings during the 36 days she was away. This was again an indication of Rahul’s reluctance to take charge. When the Hazare agitation was at its peak in August, Rahul led a delegation of MPs to the Prime Minister to talk about the land acquisition bill. Impatient with his disconnect, the MPs surrounded him at 7 Race Course Road after the meeting with Manmohan and pleaded with him to step in. They complained about the Government’s mishandling of the Hazare campaign. Though Rahul spoke in Parliament the next day, he did not offer any resolution or display leadership.

What aggravates Sonia’s agony is the fact that, set against an heir apparent who is a permanent work in progress is a prime minister who has lost his elan. When Manmohan complained that the Opposition was trying to destabilise his government, Janata Party leader Subramanian Swamy asked, "Does he mean opposition within or outside the Congress?"

The dominant feeling within the Cabinet is that there is a growing need for a political Prime Minister. "All the crises have been political, not economic. We don’t need an economist, we need a politician," says a Congress Cabinet minister. There are also few takers for Manmohan’s economic policies. "The two arms of the Prime Minister are the PMO and the Planning Commission. Both are out of sync with the party," says the Cabinet minister.

He rattles off a list of Congress Cabinet ministers-Kamal Nath, Jairam Ramesh and M. Veerappa Moily-who are upset with Planning Commission chief Montek Singh Ahluwalia. "To solve the problems of the rural poor, the Planning Commission has hired a team of the urban rich," adds a party general secretary. "Once Pulok Chatterji joins the PMO, then the party will have its man in place there. Right now, there is no connect between the party and the Prime Minister’s Office," he said. Added to this leadership vacuum is the mystery about Sonia’s illness.

Since the party has not yet been officially briefed about it, the field has been left open to conspiracy theorists. "Even public personalities are entitled to privacy in so far as their personal life is concerned," says Congress spokesperson Manish Tewari. Sonia has never functioned as a ‘visible’ leader; yet never was the need for her party to get a glimpse of its president greater.

Her spin doctors organised a well-choreographed meeting of the Central Election Committee on September 15, ostensibly to discuss candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls. It provided an ideal showcase of a leader in control. When the Prime Minister drove up to 10 Janpath, she was at the door to receive him and see him off. "She looked at the candidate list and her immediate reaction was why there were so few Congressmen on it," said a senior Congress leader, pointing out that most of the candidates were former BSP and SP politicians. "Rahul then said he would talk to the Youth Congress to suggest some names," added the Congress leader. What he didn’t voice was the relief that his party president seemed ‘okay’. Later, Congress General Secretary Janardhan Dwivedi told the media that "she looked normal... but it will take her a little time to fully recover".

Until the Pranab vs Chidambaram letter bomb landed in her in-tray, Sonia was content with routine party work such as nominating PCC teams for Goa and Maharashtra and taking a decision on whether the Congress should go it alone in the Tamil Nadu local elections. She has also begun meeting Cabinet ministers and party officials, managing four-five meetings daily.

"She is watching a lot more television than she does normally and is worried about party turf wars," says a Congress leader. Considering the malady afflicting the Government, it could be a long while before the Congress president sees something she likes on TV.

news.n_title: How the new Indian tourist is travelling more than ever before
news.n_description: Instead of just annual vacations, people are travelling more frequently for shorter breaks. Travel industry experts explain the trend

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Historically, travel in India meant families going together, mostly to visit their grandparents, or travel largely confined to summer and winter vacations.

Today, instead of one or two annual vacations, people are travelling more frequently for shorter breaks, whether it is weekend getaways, long-weekend breaks or spontaneous trips, along with one or two long holidays, says Rajesh Magow, co-founder and group CEO, MakeMyTrip. On MakeMyTrip’s platform, people book an average of two to seven trips a year.

What has helped is improved highways, expressways and rising private vehicle ownership, which have made destinations within a few hours of major cities accessible, encouraging road trips and exploration of lesser-known locations.

These shorter trip or staycations typically last two or three nights, with two nights being more common. These are weekend or long-weekend trips wherein some travellers may take a Friday or Monday off. This is different from summer and winter vacations, which generally last more than four nights, says Magow.

Within the staycation category, a new category of celebration travel is emerging rapidly, says Magow, where families or friends travel together to celebrate a birthday or anniversary. “Earlier, people would go to their nani or dadi’s place to celebrate a family occasion. Now they take them along for milestone birthdays and anniversaries,” he notes.

The nature of travel has also changed. “Holidays have become a regular lifestyle choice rather than an occasional annual indulgence,” says S.D. Nandakumar, president and country head, holidays and corporate tours, SOTC Travel.

The frequency of travelling, though, is directly linked to the household income. “Every income segment travels,” says Magow, adding that every household that can afford it wants to travel today. “The choice is no longer between travelling and not travelling. The inflection point is an annual household income of about Rs 5 lakh, at which households take at least one or two trips a year. The frequency increases with rising income,” he says.

No surprise then, India recorded 4,287 million domestic tourist visits in 2025, up from 2,322 million in 2019, according to the ministry of tourism’s India Tourism Data Compendium 2025.

Urban travellers are looking for experiential travel whether it is nature-led, adventure, wildlife, wellness, premium or interest-based holidays, while travellers from emerging markets and smaller cities are exploring new destinations, often with family and through value-led packages, says Nandakumar. “But across markets, comfort, convenience, safety and value remain important considerations.”

Digital booking platforms have helped too by simplifying the discovery and booking process and helping people plan even at the last minute, easing the process of planning frequently. On MakeMyTrip, 45-50 per cent of ticket bookings or travel plans happen within 48 hours, suggesting that Indians are not necessarily the most-advanced planners. “A very small proportion of our population really plans trips months in advance,” he says.

news.n_title: How Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana' raises new questions, adds contexts but sticks to epic's core
news.n_description: 'Ramayana: Part 1' should be judged not only by how faithfully it repeats our old memories but also how many new meanings it adds for a new generation

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Putting ‘Ram Katha’ on screen is not merely an exercise in lending visual grandeur to an epic but also a responsibility while entering into dialogue with the memory, faith and cultural consciousness of Indians, what with the many interpretations that have evolved over centuries.

That is why making a Ramayana film is as attractive as risky. Viewers do not come to theatres simply to watch; they bring along their own imageries of Ram, Sita, Lakshman and Ravan. They carry Tulsidas and Valmiki, folk tales and Ramlilas, and memories of Ramanand Sagar’s Ramayan on television. In the backdrop of these memories and expectations, director Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana: Part 1 makes an ambitious attempt to pitch a cinematic language of its own.

The film is impressive, grand and wildly ambitious. Above all, it leaves room for debate. A contemporary retelling of a tale is meaningful only when it goes beyond restaging familiar episodes in new visuals and brings out the questions buried within. In this respect, the film appears to make some bold attempts.

Ranbir Kapoor’s Ram is restrained, gentle and dignified. Accepting him as Ram is difficult at first, but by the time the Ram-Kaikeyi exchange occurs, the audience begins to see Ram in him. Still, the expectations are so enormous that every gesture, line and expression is bound to be measured against established images. Aware of the challenge, Ranbir seems, in places, to be visibly striving.

As Lakshman, Ravi Dubey is energetic, fluid and playful. His character has a natural dynamism that strikes an interesting balance with Ram’s comparatively calm persona. Lakshman is not merely Ram’s younger brother or someone who carries out his orders. He has impulse, questions and, at times, dissent. Ravi’s performance gives that energy room.

The most natural presence in the film is Sai Pallavi’s. Her Sita is meaningful, sharp and effective. There is an ease in her presence that invites us to see the character as a living person rather than an artificial ideal. Tiwari has not presented Sita merely as the embodiment of endurance and sacrifice. With her independent mind, capacity for judgment and self-respect, she has been the indispensable centre of Ram Katha.

The hints of her agency and thoughtfulness in the film provoke real curiosity. The portrayal of a Sita running, wielding weapons, and asking the sage to recite a hymn to confirm his identity before she offers alms is an attempt to move beyond the familiar image. The full expanse of her personality and ideas, however, remains yet to be explored.

But the performance most talked about is Yash’s as Ravan—formidable, towering and overpowering. His personality has the theatrical amplitude one expects of this character, and his presence carries both allure and dread.

It is being said on social media that Ravan overpowers Ram in the film. Does he really? To answer this, one must first grasp a fundamental distinction. Yash may outshine Ranbir but Ravan does not overpower Ram. An actor’s performance being more impactful and the character he plays dominating the story’s central hero are two different things. Likewise, a character does not dominate another simply by being given more screen-time or a grander presentation. The effectiveness of a performance and the ideological centrality of a character should not be weighed on the same scale.

Now consider Arun Govil’s performance. As king Dashrath, he is not on screen for long, yet his acting is seasoned, sensitive and poignant. The language of experience etched on his face suits the character perfectly. His casting also evokes an intriguing cultural memory: he once played Ram on television and left a lasting image in viewers’ minds. Now he returns as the father of a Ram from another generation. When Ram departs for exile and Govil collapses calling out his son’s name, the performance eclipses the grandeur of the screen. Equally powerful is Sheeba Chaddha as Manthara.

In all of this, one person deserves special praise: Sharad Kelkar, who provides the Hindi dubbing for Ravan. His voice is the very life-breath of the character. It shows what a voice can do for the cinematic presence of a larger-than-life figure.

Director Tiwari is imaginative, accomplished, experimental and a visionary of scale. He has attempted to recreate on the big screen a story about which Indian audiences already know a great deal. The challenge then lies in making people experience it anew. His effort, together with producer Namit Malhotra’s, to take an Indian story to the global stage largely succeeds.

The writers, researchers and advisors, such as Shreyas Jain, Shridhar Raghavan and Bodhisattva, also play an important role here. The film’s ideological foundation reflects an effort to accept contemporaneity while keeping the soul of tradition intact. Presenting a story in today’s time requires admitting new questions and contexts into it, but this must not be done by displacing its essential sensibility.

Some of the film’s dialogues provoke debate at precisely this level. As Ravan speaks of an egalitarian society, some viewers would be offended while others may applaud. But the question is not merely that Ravan spoke of equality. The real question is whether he actually managed to build such a society.

Do a person’s ideological declarations match his conduct? Should personal ambition encompass social ambition or should social ambition leave adequate room for personal ambitions? Ravan’s character offers an opportunity to raise these questions. Listening to an antagonist’s ideas and agreeing with them is one thing; evaluating his entire personality and deeds is another. That the film makes space for such questions is one of its significant achievements.

As for shortcomings, they exist too, as in every film. Criticism is necessary but criticism cannot mean predetermined rejection. It is also possible that some dialogues and scenes will grate while others satisfy; that some portrayals will challenge familiar assumptions while others fail to reach the expected depth.

What one sees here, in essence, is an attempt to forge a cinematic vision out of the many traditions and interpretations of Ram Katha. We must recognise that time has moved far beyond the era of Sagar’s Ramayan. The language of cinema has changed, audience expectations too have, and so have the contexts in which we view and understand the story.

Ramayana: Part 1 should be judged not only by how faithfully it repeats our old memories but also by how many new meanings it adds for a new generation. The film does not answer every question nor does it live up to expectations everywhere. Even so, there is much in it that one accepts with ease. Perhaps that is because the storyline converses with its time, raises new questions and adds new contexts, yet never strays from its core.

news.n_title: Kuppam to Pulivendula: How Jagan Reddy, Chandrababu stormed rival bastions in local polls
news.n_description: As the YRSCP alleges irregularities in polling and counting, Andhra Pradesh CM Chandrababu Naidu says the results reaffirm voters' faith in NDA

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Telugu Desam Party (TDP) chief N. Chandrababu Naidu suffered a shocker five years ago when Jagan Mohan Reddy’s Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP) stormed Kuppam, Naidu’s electoral citadel of about four decades in Andhra Pradesh.

Now, Naidu’s party has extracted retribution by claiming the Pulivendula municipality and dominating the zilla parishad territorial constituencies (ZPTCs) and mandal parishad territorial constituencies (MPTCs) in local body polls in Reddy’s home-ground Kadapa district.

While Kuppam in Chittoor district has been Naidu’s assembly constituency since 1989, Pulivendula was represented by the late Congress chief minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy earlier and, since 2014, his son Jagan Reddy.

Of the 40 wards in the Pulivendula ULB (urban local body), the TDP won 34 wards in polls held on November 1 while the YSRCP managed only three despite Reddy camping in the town before and during the voting. Of the 16 ZPTC seats in Kadapa district that includes Pulivendula, the TDP bagged 12, the Jana Sena Party two and YSRCP two.

In 2021, when Reddy was in power, the YSRCP had breached Kuppam too as the party swept the ZPTC and MPTC polls statewide. In the November 2021 ULB polls, the TDP was defeated in the Kuppam municipality too, where the YSRCP won 19 out of the 25 wards and occupied the chairman’s post.

Naidu had then charged the YSRCP of deploying bogus voters to subvert the mandate in Kuppam and other civic bodies. The TDP chief had even accused then chief minister Reddy and his party leaders of “committing midnight murder of democracy by getting TDP polling agents and leaders arrested hours before the election”.

Now, it is Reddy’s turn to make similar accusations. On November 3, when the ULB poll results were declared, Reddy posted on social media that Naidu, the police and the State Election Commission “have demonstrated how to win an election spectacularly by ensuring that the Opposition never gets a chance to compete”.

Reddy charged that from filing of nominations to polling agents to the voting and counting itself, the various stages of the election were systematically compromised: in his words “hijacked, “obstructed”, “rigged”, “manipulated”.

On November 1 too, Reddy staged a protest outside the returning officer’s office in Pulivendula, strongly objecting to YSRCP polling agents “being prevented from entering polling booths during the municipal election”. On November 9, after the final tally of ZPTC and MPTC poll results emerged, Reddy posted on X again, calling Naidu “rigging master”.

Rubbishing the accusations, TDP leaders say the results reaffirm Andhra Pradesh voters’ faith in Naidu and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).

In a state that witnessed no bypolls in the past two and a half years, the local body elections are seen as serving as a mid-term assessment of the NDA government. Assembly polls are due in 2029.

Naidu is elated with the results, terming it “as reflecting people's support for good governance”. Speaking to the media in Amaravati on November 9, he said the NDA had demonstrated overwhelming dominance in the ULB elections: out of 100 mayor and chairperson positions, the alliance won 94, including 12 of the 13 mayor positions and 82 of the 87 chairperson positions. Of these, the TDP secured 70 mayor and chairperson positions, JSP 20 and the BJP four. The Opposition YSRCP won only four and Independents two seats.

The chief minister said the NDA won 575 of the 659 ZPTC seats, securing a lead in 27 of 28 districts. The YSRCP could win more ZPTC seats than the ruling alliance only in Alluri Sitarama Raju district. The party failed to win even a single ZPTC seat in seven districts of Anakapalli, Konaseema, Kakinada, Markapuram, Palnadu, West Godavari and Visakhapatnam, noted Naidu.

Naidu also dwelt on the results in Kadapa-Pulivendula, Reddy’s home turf. “In Pulivendula, we secured the municipal chairperson’s position with a majority of 13,875 votes, winning 37 of 40 wards. In Kadapa Municipal Corporation, we won with a majority of 65,588 votes, securing 64 of the 66 wards,” he said.

“People in Kadapa district have put an end to rowdy politics,” Naidu said, adding that all nine ULBs in the district were won by the alliance while the YSRCP was restricted to only nine of 345 wards in the YSR-Kadapa district.

As Reddy alleges irregularities in polling and manipulations in counting as having tainted the local body elections, Naidu said the results demonstrated that elections conducted democratically and freely would produce such welcome outcomes.
