news.n_title: Why Ladakh-Kargil groups want hill council polls boycotted-deferred
news.n_description: The December 4 polls have prompted calls for an indefinite protest over unresolved issues of delimitation and constitutional safeguards for the Union territory

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
The Ladakh Union territory administration has announced polls for the eight hill councils on December 4 despite demands from Leh and Kargil-based groups for a deferment of the process, including the panchayat and municipal elections slated for November 21.

Leh-based groups had already called for a boycott of the elections, citing seasonal migration of nearly 25 per cent of the local population, especially senior citizens, extreme weather and unresolved issues over delimitation and constitutional safeguards for the region. Soon after the poll notifications were issued on November 10, the Ladakh bodies announced an “indefinite dharna” beginning November 12.

The Union territory administration, headed by Ladakh lieutenant governor V.K. Saxena, on November 10 issued a gazette notification calling upon all 100 “constituencies of all the eight” Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs) “to elect members for the purpose of constituting new councils”. Soon after, a separate notification announcing the schedule for elections to the eight hill councils was issued by the State Election Commission. According to it, polling for electing members to the new hill councils across all eight districts of Ladakh would be held on December 4.

The entire process, including the results, is to be completed by December 8. November 17 has been fixed as the last date for filing nominations, November 18 for scrutiny and November 20 for withdrawal of candidature.

The notifications were issued on a day Kargil region was observing a complete shutdown, demanding postponement of the LAHDC elections as well as municipal and panchayat polls until the winter season had passed.

Taking a hard line, three influential Leh-based organisations—the Ladakh Buddhist Association (LBA), Ladakh Gonpa Association, and Nambardar Association—have issued a call to boycott the panchayat and municipal polls. “Whichever elections are being announced, including the hill council elections, will be boycotted by the people of Ladakh,” Chering Dorjay Lakrook, president of LBA, told INDIA TODAY.

Lakrook is also convener of the Apex Body Leh (ABL), which along with the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) is leading the agitation for Ladakh’s rights as well as constitutional safeguards to the region’s autonomy.

The ABL and KDA were also leading the now-stalled talks with the central government on these issues. As the negotiations stalled, the Centre proceeded with a sweeping restructuring of local governance in the Union territory, prompting suspicion that the region’s political future was being reshaped without its people’s consent.

“How are they (Ladakh administration) conducting elections without [the participation of] people? They are forcing it,” charged Lakrook. He said people had strong reservations about the delimitation process based upon which the hill councils have been constituted.

Lakrook said there was palpable anger over the delay in making public the report of the judicial inquiry commission that probed the September 24, 2025 violence in Ladakh. Four people were killed in police firing on protesters, who were demanding statehood and Sixth Schedule protections for the Union territory. He added that people have also been demanding a rollback of the new liquor policy and designation of Ladakh as a dry Union territory.

Lakrook said ABL had decided to launch an indefinite sit-in protest from November 12 over all contentious issues, including the delay in resumption of stalled talks by the Centre.

In his statement about the Kargil shutdown on November 10, KDA convenor Sajjad Kargili said the notifications, including election schedules, had been issued without consulting local people and that “unilateral” decisions were unacceptable. “The reason behind holding this shutdown is that attempts are being made to weaken democracy in Ladakh. Conspiracies are being hatched to snatch our land. Every day, we are witnessing an unending process of orders and notifications from the administration without the consent of local people. While the people of Ladakh are concerned about delimitation, gerrymandering is on,” Kargili said in a video statement on X.

Ladakh’s Lok Sabha MP Mohammad Haneefa Jan has also written to the lieutenant governor to reconsider the proposed polls. The letter cites seasonal migration, extreme weather and the need for a comprehensive revision of electoral rolls.

“The credibility of the democratic institutions rests not merely on the timely conduct of elections but, more importantly, on ensuring that every eligible citizen can participate freely, fairly and without undue hardship,” stated the letter. “Holding elections during this period, without adequately addressing these circumstances, could deprive many eligible voters of a fair opportunity to participate in a democratic process.”

Responding to the reservations expressed by various groups across Ladakh, chief secretary Ashish Kundra argued that weather conditions should not prevent people from exercising their franchise. He cited that even schools in Ladakh remain open until December 15 whereas the poll date was December 4.

“If children can go to school, I don’t think adults cannot go out to vote,” Kundra said, describing the hill council elections as a “watershed moment” for the region. He urged people to demonstrate their commitment to the democratic process by turning up to vote. The chief secretary claimed that feedback received from the districts had indicated broad public satisfaction with the delimitation process.

news.n_title: Bombs, blockades, arson rock Bangladesh as Hasina's planned return draws closer
news.n_description: Crude bomb blasts, arson attacks and road blockades have rocked Bangladesh over the past few weeks. The violence comes ahead of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina's planned return from exile in India, with authorities blaming her Awami League and its supporters for the unrest. Bangladesh appears to have headed into another period of turmoil even before Hasina set foot in the country.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Crude bombs exploding on the streets, buses going up in flames, highways blocked and protesters clashing with police. Bangladesh is once again witnessing violence in Dhaka, Gazipur, Gopalganj, Shariatpur and other districts. Security forces have made hundreds of arrests. Behind the unrest, Bangladeshi authorities see the hand of a familiar force, the Awami League and ousted PM Sheikh Hasina. The violence comes less than a month before Hasina's planned return to Bangladesh from exile in India, which has raised fears of more mayhem in a country still recovering from the deadly protests that forced her out in August 2024.

The latest incident was reported early on Thursday (November 12), when the house of Nusrat Tabassum, an NCP MP from a reserved women's seat representing Kushtia, was set on fire after being allegedly firebombed by Awami League activists around midnight.

A day earlier, on Wednesday (November 11), two buses and a truck were set ablaze in Dhaka, while a Grameen Bank branch was torched in Pabna Sadar, according to The Daily Star. The incidents followed at least 22 cases of arson and crude bomb explosions across Bangladesh on November 9 and 10, reported the Dhaka-based newspaper The Business Standard.

At least 15 crude bomb explosions took place in Dhaka alone between November 1 and 8, according to media reports.

While Bangladesh is no stranger to large-scale street violence, the timing of these incidents is significant. Hasina, who has been living in India since leaving Bangladesh in August 2024, announced in August this year that she intended to return to her country by December. Her return could trigger fresh turmoil as she faces a death sentence, her Awami League remains banned, and her supporters and opponents remain divided over her future.

After Hasina's ouster, the Muhammad Yunus-led interim administration banned Hasina's Awami League and initiated legal proceedings over the deadly crackdown on protesters. A tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia in November 2025. Despite the conviction, which she has rejected as politically motivated, Hasina now intends to return to Bangladesh. Amid the buzz of her return, fresh bomb blasts, arson and unrest have gripped the country.

The Tarique Rahman-led BNP government appeared to have brought a temporary lull in Bangladesh's political violence after the February 2026 elections, with an October UK government report noting an improvement in the country's security situation. That relative calm now appears to be giving way to renewed unrest. Since Hasina announced at a press conference in New Delhi in August that she intended to return to Bangladesh by December, the country has witnessed a spate of crude bomb blasts, arson attacks and clashes with security forces.

The incidents have become particularly frequent in late October and early November, coinciding with protests by garment factory workers demanding higher wages and escalating tensions in the country's industrial areas.

BOMBS EXPLODE, BUSES BURN ACROSS BANGLADESH

The latest wave of violence in several cities and towns in Bangladesh began gathering momentum in late October.

On October 30, Dhaka-based The Business Standard reported several crude bomb explosions near the Kalabagan bus stand in the capital. Police subsequently arrested four people and recovered 13 explosive devices.

The attacks continued into November.

According to The Daily Star, at least 15 crude bomb explosions were reported in Dhaka between November 1 and 8.

Explosions occurred near the Agargaon metro station, Dhanmondi Government Boys' High School, the July Memorial Museum and Rajarbagh Police Lines, among other locations.

On November 5, a police constable was injured when a crude bomb was hurled at a patrol vehicle near Dhaka's Kurmitola General Hospital.

The violence subsequently spread beyond the capital. Buses have been torched, and rude bombs have been hurled in Dhaka's outskirts and several other districts.

The Business Standard reported that 19 buses were set ablaze and explosions occurred at 27 locations between November 7 and 9. At least 22 more incidents involving arson and crude bomb explosions were reported across the country on November 9 and 10.

The attacks have caused multiple injuries and arrests. At least one person, a bus driver, died after becoming trapped inside a parked bus that was set on fire in Faridpur.

AWAMI LEAGUE'S BLOCKADE ADDS TO UNREST

The unrest took a more overtly political turn on November 10, when the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL), the student wing of Hasina's Awami League, called for a nationwide blockade.

The organisation had announced the programme through its Facebook page on November 9, urging supporters to enforce the shutdown across Bangladesh.

In Shariatpur, Awami League and Chhatra League activists blocked the Dhaka-Bhanga Expressway near the Padma Bridge toll plaza. Protesters wielded sticks, exploded crude bombs and vandalised trucks. Traffic remained disrupted for nearly an hour, leaving hundreds of vehicles stranded.

In Gopalganj's Tungipara, Chhatra League activists blocked roads and set tyres on fire, triggering clashes with police.

Protesters vandalised and torched a police vehicle after security personnel attempted to disperse them using tear gas and rubber bullets.

Road blockades were also reported in Kashiani and Gopalganj town, prompting authorities to deploy six platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), the country's foremost paramilitary force.

GARMENT WORKERS' PROTESTS FUEL VIOLENCE IN BANGLADESH

The reported mobilisation by the Awami League and its outfits has coincided with another major source of unrest, the protests by workers in Bangladesh's ready-made garment industry. Workers have been demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from Tk 12,500 to Tk 30,000. The last wage revision took place in 2023.

The demonstrations intensified in late October and early November, particularly in Dhaka, Gazipur and Savar.

Workers repeatedly clashed with police, while vehicles, factories, warehouses and other properties were vandalised or set ablaze.

Hundreds of garment factories were forced to suspend production amid the disruptions. Police subsequently filed cases over attacks on officers, vandalism, crude bomb explosions and the torching of a police vehicle. Several people were arrested, including suspects alleged to have links with the Awami League.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused former Awami League ministers, lawmakers and factory owners associated with the party of exploiting workers' grievances to create instability.

However, workers' demands over wages remain a separate and significant cause of the demonstrations.

AUTHORITIES BLAME HASINA'S AWAMI LEAGUE FOR VIOLENCE

Bangladeshi authorities have repeatedly pointed fingers at the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations over the recent spate of violence, alleging that the party's supporters are attempting to destabilise the country.

On November 8, Additional Inspector General of Police (Crime and Operations) Mohammad Sayedur Rahman directly accused the Awami League of orchestrating the crude bomb explosions and bus arson attacks. "These incidents are clearly intended to destabilise the government and create panic among the public," The Daily Star quoted him as saying.

The police have also made a series of arrests in connection with the attacks. According to The Daily Star, at least 21 people were arrested over crude bomb explosions between November 1 and 7, while 898 people linked to the Awami League were arrested in separate ongoing police drives during the same period.

Five Awami League affiliates were also arrested over explosions in Dhaka in the 24 hours preceding November 8. On November 10, police spokesperson Mohammad Akhtar Hossain told the Associated Press that at least 33 people had been arrested in Dhaka, with further arrests elsewhere. He said those involved were linked to a banned organisation and its affiliated groups, adding that some had allegedly been paid to carry out the attacks.

The allegations of political involvement have also extended to the garment workers' unrest. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed alleged that former Awami League leaders and factory owners linked to the outlawed party were exploiting workers' grievances to create instability.

PM Rahman's Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman subsequently acknowledged that the banned Awami League was linked to violence surrounding the protests. However, he explicitly rejected the suggestion that the unrest was part of an attempt to facilitate Sheikh Hasina's return in December.

VIOLENCE HEAD OF SHEIKH HASINA'S PLANNED RETURN

The developments come as Hasina steps up her efforts to return to Bangladesh from India, where she has been living since fleeing Dhaka in August 2024. At a press conference in New Delhi on August 5, she said, describing it as Bangladesh's "victory month".

She reiterated the commitment in subsequent interviews, including one with the Associated Press earlier this month, saying she intended to return despite the risk of arrest, imprisonment and even death. For context, Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by the country's International Crimes Tribunal for Crime Against Humanity.

On November 9, her lawyers also approached the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi seeking a new passport and national identity card to facilitate her return. However, Dhaka rejected the request, insisting that Hasina must be brought back through the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty rather than return on her own terms.

Hasina's planned return comes amid deep political divisions. The Awami League is banned, and a death sentence is hanging over her. Her arrival could reignite tensions between her supporters and security forces, which raises fears of another wave of unrest.

With Hasina's planned return drawing closer, the renewed violence has emerged as a major challenge for the Tarique Rahman government, which had promised to restore stability after years of political turmoil. While authorities have blamed the Awami League for much of the unrest, the garment workers' protests suggest that economic grievances are also fuelling tensions in the nation. For Bangladesh, the latest turmoil has revived fears of another period of instability even before Hasina sets foot in the country.

news.n_title: Brazil legend Ronaldinho comes out of retirement, joins Italian club Ravenna FC
news.n_description: Brazilian football legend Ronaldinho is set to return to competitive action after more than a decade, joining Italian Serie C side Ravenna FC as both a player and shareholder. The 46-year-old will make his comeback against Forli on November 15, with the Brazilian targeting his 300th career goal.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Brazilian football icon Ronaldinho is set to return to competitive football after more than a decade away from the professional game, with the 46-year-old preparing to pull on the Ravenna FC jersey in Italy's third tier.

The former Barcelona and AC Milan star will make his comeback for Ravenna in their Serie C derby against Forli on November 15. The club confirmed the date in October, bringing an end to months of speculation over whether the Brazilian would actually feature on the pitch after joining the club earlier this year.

Ronaldinho's return is particularly special because he will be involved with Ravenna in two capacities: as a player and a shareholder. The Brazilian signed for the Italian club in June and subsequently acquired a stake in the team, which is owned by his friend Ignazio Cipriani.

Also Read: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino: Has the moment finally arrived?

The comeback will mark his first competitive appearance since September 2015, when he turned out for Brazilian club Fluminense. Although he officially announced his retirement in 2018, the prospect of seeing one of football's most entertaining players back in action has generated considerable excitement.

RONALDINHO EYES ONE LAST MOMENT OF MAGIC

The comeback also gives Ronaldinho an opportunity to achieve one final milestone. The Brazilian is aiming to score the 300th goal of his professional career, having finished his playing days with 299 goals.

Ravenna's fixture against Forli at the Stadio Bruno Benelli will provide the stage for his much-anticipated return. The club announced that the Brazilian would wear its colours in the derby, describing the occasion as a moment that would turn the world's attention towards the stadium.

Ronaldinho, meanwhile, has expressed his excitement about returning to the game. Following his signing, he said he could not wait to play with the ball again and write a new story with the club. For the former Brazil international, football has always been about joy, and he hopes to bring that spirit to Ravenna.

The Brazilian's association with the club is also part of an ambitious project to raise its profile. His presence as a shareholder and player is expected to bring international attention to the Italian side and help strengthen its connection with supporters.

Ronaldinho, of course, needs little introduction. He was part of Brazil's 2002 FIFA World Cup-winning team and won the Ballon d'Or in 2005 after a remarkable spell at Barcelona. He also represented Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan, dazzling fans with his dribbling, creativity, outrageous skills and trademark smile.

At Barcelona, he played a key role in the club's rise to prominence in the mid-2000s, winning two La Liga titles and the UEFA Champions League in 2006.

Now, more than 11 years after his last competitive appearance, the Brazilian is preparing to return to the pitch. Ravenna's supporters will hope that the man who made football look effortless can deliver one more magical moment — and perhaps find that elusive 300th goal.

news.n_description: A video shot by someone at Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran's wedding celebrations has gone viral on social media, showing Superstar Rajinikanth dancing to Petta's Marana Mass and Vettaiyan's Manasilaayo.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
After Jailer’s massive theatrical run, Superstar Rajinikanth is back in the spotlight. This time for his dance moves at the wedding celebrations of his nephew, music composer Anirudh Ravichander. A video from Anirudh and Kavya Maran's wedding festivities in Greece has gone viral on social media, showing the actor dancing to two of the groom's popular compositions.

The video captures Rajinikanth dancing to Marana Mass from his 2019 film Petta. As the energetic number gradually transitions into Manasilaayo from Vettaiyan (2024), the superstar continues to groove, enjoying the moment as those around him join in the celebrations.

#KavyaMaran #SuperstarRajinikanth https://t.co/uoc7FfkiGF

— Pras (@hvbhat) November 11, 2026

Both songs were composed by Anirudh, who has delivered several popular tracks for Rajinikanth over the years. The footage, recorded by a guest attending the private celebrations, offers a rare glimpse into the festivities. Neither family has officially released the video, which has since been widely circulated on social media.

Adding to the charm of the clip is the gathering around the superstar. Rajinikanth is seen dancing at the centre, surrounded by members of both families. Sun Group chairman Kalanithi Maran and Anirudh's father, Ravi Raghavendra, are among those present. Rajinikanth's daughter Soundarya is seen to his left, while the newlyweds, Anirudh and Kavya, are on his right. The sight of the couple celebrating as Rajinikanth dances to Anirudh's music has made the video a talking point among fans.

Anirudh and Kavya got married in an intimate destination wedding in Greece on November 11. The celebrations reportedly began with a traditional Nichayathartham (engagement ceremony) on November 10, followed by the wedding attended by close family members and select guests.

Rajinikanth reportedly travelled to Greece with his wife Latha and daughter Aishwarya. Former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin and Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin were also among the prominent guests.

The couple are expected to host a reception on November 21 at ITC Grand Chola in Chennai, with prominent personalities from cinema, politics and business expected to attend.

news.n_title: Fired 15 rounds, said Happy Diwali: Faridabad murder over parking caught on CCTV
news.n_description: CCTV footage shows Monu Sharma confronting Paramjit Dhankhar before allegedly shooting him in Faridabad. The clips detail how a parking dispute escalated into a fatal attack.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
CCTV footage has emerged showing the moments leading up to the killing of Paramjit Dhankhar, a former senior vice-president at Tech Mahindra, in Faridabad's Sector 21C on the evening of Dhanteras, two days before Diwali.

The footage shows the accused, Monu Sharma, calling Dhankhar out of his first-floor flat on the pretext of discussing a parking issue before opening fire on him.

The video also captures an exchange between the two men shortly before the shooting, as well as the final moments when Dhankhar reaches the building's main gate and confronts the accused again.

The incident took place on November 5, 2026, and the accused was Mohan alias Monu Sharma, who lived in the same building.

He was later arrested by the Faridabad Crime Branch after fleeing with his family. Police had said the accused fired 15–16 rounds from his licenced pistol, leaving Dhankar with eight to nine bullet injuries.

CCTV SHOWS ACCUSED'S EXCHANGE WITH VICTIM BEFORE FIRING

In the first CCTV clip, Sharma is seen approaching Dhankar, who comes down to the parking area with his son. The accused reportedly began the conversation by asking Dhankar twice whether he knew what a widow was and whether he believed in it.

Dhankar appears confused by the question and asks him what has happened. Sharma then accuses him of getting three people to assault him.

Dhankar is seen trying to pacify Sharma, folding his hands and telling him that he had not arranged for anyone to beat him. He also attempted to ask the accused what the dispute was about and how long he had been living in the building.

However, Sharma refuses to engage in the conversation and repeatedly tells Dhankar that he does not want to speak to him.

At one point, Dhankar tells him that if he does not want to talk, there is no point continuing the discussion. His son also attempts to intervene, but Dhankar stops him from getting involved.

The footage then shows Sharma gesturing towards the son and asking him to come forward. He subsequently asks Dhankar whether he believes in God, pulls out a pistol from his pocket and opens fire at him. Dhankar's son is seen running away from the spot.

ACCUSED FIRES MORE SHOTS NEAR BUILDING'S MAIN GATE

Another CCTV clip captures the moments after the initial shooting near the building's main entrance.

Dhankar is seen reaching the gate, apparently seeking help. When Sharma approaches him from behind, Dhankar grabs the accused by his collar and brings him to the ground.

During this confrontation, Dhankar's mother arrives at the spot and calls out to his daughter-in-law.

The footage then shows Sharma firing four more rounds at Dhankar. The accused is also heard abusing him and saying, "Happy Diwali," before fleeing from the spot.

The CCTV footage provides a sequence of events leading up to the killing and captures the confrontation between the two men at different locations inside the residential complex.

WHAT HAPPENED IN THE FARIDABAD PARKING DISPUTE KILLING?

Dhankar was shot dead in Faridabad's Sector 21C on the evening of Dhanteras, two days before Diwali. He had returned to Faridabad from Singapore shortly before the incident to attend his nephew's wedding.

According to the earlier report, Dhankar had left Tech Mahindra around two months before the killing to join a Singapore-based multinational company in a senior position. He lived with his wife, son and daughter in the building, while Sharma resided on the third floor.

Police said an argument over parking escalated, following which Sharma opened fire using his licensed pistol.

The two families also reportedly had a history of disagreements, including an altercation involving Dhankar's son and the accused over a dog a few days before the shooting.

Sharma fled with his family after the incident but was subsequently arrested by the Crime Branch.

news.n_title: Man United sack head coach Carrick after poor run leaves club in relegation zone
news.n_description: Manchester United sack head coach Michael Carrick after poor run leaves club in relegation zone

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Manchester United have parted ways with head coach Michael Carrick following a disappointing start to the 2026-27 Premier League season, bringing an end to his second spell at Old Trafford.

The decision comes after a difficult opening to the campaign, with United languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table after 10 matches. The Red Devils have managed just one victory during that period, leaving them facing an unexpected relegation battle and prompting the club hierarchy to make a change in the dugout.

United confirmed Carrick's departure in an official statement, thanking the former midfielder for his contribution to the club and acknowledging his achievements during his return last season.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," the statement read.

The club also confirmed that it intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible. However, no replacement has been announced, with the immediate focus likely to be on finding a candidate capable of turning around United's fortunes.

Carrick's departure marks a disappointing end to a tenure that had begun with considerable promise. Having returned to Manchester in January, the former England international initially took charge of the first team and made an immediate impact, guiding the club through an impressive run of results.

CARRICK'S PROMISING RETURN

Carrick rejoined United in January 2026 and helped revive their campaign after a difficult period. He guided the Red Devils to a third-place finish in the Premier League, winning 12 of their remaining 17 matches during the 2025-26 season.

United also accumulated the highest points tally in the league during that period, underlining the impact Carrick made after taking charge. His work in the dugout convinced the club to hand him the head coach's position on a permanent basis ahead of the new campaign.

The appointment was seen as an opportunity to build on the momentum generated during the closing months of the previous season. Carrick, who spent 12 years at Old Trafford as a player, was familiar with the club's expectations and had earned considerable goodwill among supporters.

However, the start of the 2026-27 campaign has been a different story altogether.

United have struggled to find consistency, with their lack of victories exposing problems at both ends of the pitch. Their position in 19th place after 10 matches has intensified the pressure on Carrick, with the club unwilling to allow the situation to deteriorate further.

The decision to part ways with the 45-year-old comes despite his impressive work last season, highlighting the urgency surrounding United's current predicament.

UNITED BEGIN SUCCESSOR SEARCH

In its statement, Manchester United were keen to acknowledge Carrick's contribution and his association with the club, describing him as a legend who had maintained the highest standards of dedication and professionalism.

"Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club," the statement added.

The club also expressed its appreciation for his leadership and achievements during the previous campaign, which helped United secure a top-three finish and return to the UEFA Champions League.

United now face an important decision over who takes charge of the first team. With the club sitting in the relegation zone, the next appointment will carry significant pressure, particularly with little room for a lengthy rebuilding process.

While Mauricio Pochettino has been linked with the managerial position, Manchester United have not officially confirmed an appointment or named their preferred candidate.

The Argentine has considerable Premier League experience from his time at Tottenham Hotspur and has also managed Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States men's national team.

For now, United's priority will be to identify a successor who can quickly restore confidence and get the team climbing the table. Having started the season with ambitions of challenging near the top, the immediate objective has shifted towards avoiding a prolonged battle against relegation.

Carrick leaves Old Trafford with the credit of having delivered an impressive turnaround last season, but his successor will inherit a club in need of an immediate response.

news.n_title: Death threat to Kejriwal, caller poses as Bishnoi gang member to demand Rs 7 crore
news.n_description: AAP MLA Jarnail Singh said he received a phone call from a man claiming to be a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, who demanded Rs 7 crore as extortion money.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
A death threat issued in the name of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang against Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and his daughter, Harshita Kejriwal, has turned out to be a hoax, top Punjab Police sources said. The man apprehended in connection with the case is a retired clerk from Rohtak and has no links to the gangster or his network, the sources said.

The development comes days after AAP MLA Jarnail Singh alleged that a caller claiming to be a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang had threatened to kill Kejriwal and his daughter unless Rs 7 crore was paid as ransom.

The MLA from Delhi's Tilak Nagar constituency had said he received a threatening phone call and WhatsApp messages from the caller. Singh approached the Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) on November 6 and lodged a complaint, stating that the caller had identified himself as a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.

According to Singh's complaint, the caller demanded Rs 7 crore from Kejriwal and threatened to kill him and his daughter if the money was not paid.

Based on the complaint, Mohali Police registered a case under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Information Technology Act. The investigation was assigned to Inspector Sunil Kumar of the Cyber Crime Police Station.

Top Punjab Police sources said the threat was not serious and that the man apprehended had no connection with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. The threat was found to be a hoax, they added.

JARNAIL SINGH SOUGHT SECURITY FOR KEJRIWAL

In his complaint, Singh had also sought adequate security for Kejriwal and his family in view of the alleged threat.

The 58-year-old politician had received a death threat earlier in 2019, when he was serving as Delhi Chief Minister. His office had received emails threatening to kill him, following which the Chief Minister's Office lodged a complaint and the Delhi Police launched an investigation.

news.n_title: What Sonia Gandhi says and doesn't say about the Bachchan family in her book
news.n_description: Sonia Gandhi recalls how Teji and Harivansh Rai Bachchan welcomed and guided her in India. Her memoir celebrates that early warmth while leaving the families' later estrangement largely unexplained.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, takes readers back to a time when the Gandhi and Bachchan families shared a close personal bond. Long before Amitabh Bachchan became one of India's biggest film stars and Sonia Gandhi entered politics, the two families were connected through friendship, affection and years of shared history.

Interestingly, some of Sonia's warmest recollections in the book are not about Amitabh himself but his parents, poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan and his wife, Teji Bachchan. She remembers them as the people who helped her find her feet in India when she arrived from Italy in January 1968 to marry Rajiv Gandhi.

At the time, Sonia was a young woman entering an unfamiliar country, struggling with the language, customs and expectations of a new family. It was Indira Gandhi who arranged for her to stay with the Bachchans at their Delhi residence, 13 Willingdon Crescent, before her wedding.

The Bachchans were old family friends of the Nehru-Gandhis from Allahabad. Their home became Sonia's first place of comfort in India. Amitabh Bachchan, who was already friends with Rajiv, was also among those who welcomed her when she arrived at the airport.

Sonia remembers Teji Bachchan with particular affection. She describes her as a maternal figure who helped her understand Indian customs and made her feel at home. Teji looked after her when she fell ill and remained attentive to her needs. The relationship went beyond the initial hospitality. Sonia also recalls receiving gifts from her over the years, including a puppy after the death of her firstborn son, who lived for only a few hours.

In her memoir, Sonia describes Teji as someone who was always willing to help and guide her. Harivansh Rai Bachchan, meanwhile, helped her with Hindi and offered advice that stayed with her long after those early days.

Recalling her arrival in Delhi, Sonia writes: "Tiny Mrs. Bachchan, clad in a jacket and slacks, head covered in a French-style scarf, welcomed me in the porch with the sweetest of smiles and a warm embrace. I felt at once relieved and reassured."

She also remembers how Harivansh Rai Bachchan would occasionally teach her Hindi. Despite having studied English for years, she found it difficult to communicate fluently and understand Indian accents. The poet would use their brief conversations to offer her advice about navigating life in India.

One particular observation stayed with her: "You must know, Sonia beti, child, that in this country it is not what you are that counts, it is what people think you to be."

At the time, the young Sonia struggled to understand what he meant. She wondered whether his advice meant she could never truly be herself. She admits that she would often cry quietly on her way home after being dropped back by Rajiv, missing her family and the life she had left behind in Italy.

Looking back, however, she understood the wisdom in his words. In the book, she writes:

"This warning invariably left me wondering—does he mean that I can never be myself? I was I, and that's the way I was; how could I possibly show myself differently? So it was that on many occasions, after being dropped back by Rajiv, I'd shed some quiet tears and long for my home and my family. Rajiv tried to reassure me. But in later years I remembered Uncle Bachchan's words. How right he'd been - a poet and a sensitive man, having himself experienced the fickleness of the public."

From family friends to a relationship that turned distant

The warmth of these memories becomes particularly interesting when placed against the later history of the two families.

Amitabh Bachchan and Rajiv Gandhi's friendship went back to their childhood. Their families had known each other for decades, with the connection beginning in Allahabad through Harivansh Rai Bachchan's friendship with the Nehru family. The two boys grew up around each other and remained close as adults.

Rajiv was also present during some of Amitabh's most difficult moments. When the actor met with a near-fatal accident while shooting Coolie in 1982, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv were among those who stood by the Bachchan family.

Amitabh eventually entered politics in 1984, contesting the Lok Sabha election from Allahabad as a Congress candidate. He won by a massive margin, defeating former Uttar Pradesh chief minister HN Bahuguna.

However, his political journey did not last long. The Bofors controversy, which erupted in 1987 over allegations of kickbacks in the purchase of Swedish artillery guns, brought considerable political pressure on the Congress government led by Rajiv. Amitabh's name also became embroiled in the controversy, although he denied any wrongdoing. He resigned from Parliament in 1987 and later fought legal battles to clear his name.

The relationship between the two families reportedly became strained over the years. The reasons have been discussed in various accounts, with disagreements, political developments and personal differences all featuring in the history of their falling out. The distance became more apparent after Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.

There were also public indications of the strained relationship in later years. In 2004, Amitabh's wife Jaya Bachchan, by then associated with the Samajwadi Party, and Rahul Gandhi were involved in a public exchange of remarks over the relationship between the two families.

Despite this complicated history, Sonia's memoir does not dwell on the differences or offer an explanation for what went wrong.

What Sonia Gandhi leaves unsaid about Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan

Perhaps the most striking aspect of the memoir is how little space it gives to Amitabh Bachchan, considering his long association with Rajiv Gandhi and the Gandhi family.

According to a count in the book, Amitabh's name appears only three times. Jaya Bachchan, meanwhile, does not find a mention at all.

Sonia does recall Amitabh's presence during her early days in India and his friendship with Rajiv. But there is no substantial account of their relationship in the years that followed, his entry into politics, the Bofors controversy or the differences between the two families.

There is also no discussion of the relationship between the younger members of the two families or the public disagreements that emerged years later.

news.n_title: 5 interesting characters Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana forgot to celebrate
news.n_description: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana renews attention on Guha, Kevat, Urmila, Mandodari and Vibhishan. Their stories deepen the epic's exploration of friendship, devotion, sacrifice, wisdom and righteousness.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
With Ramayana: Rise of a Legend Nitesh Tiwari has brought one of India's most celebrated epics to the big screen with larger-than-life visuals, grand sequences and characters that have lived in our collective memory for generations. While Lord Rama, Goddess Sita, Lakshman and Ravana remain central to the story, the epic is also shaped by several other characters whose contributions deserve equal attention.

The Ramayana is not just the story of Ram's journey to Lanka, his battle with Ravana and his return to Ayodhya. It is also a story of friendships that crossed social boundaries, sacrifices that went unnoticed, difficult moral choices and people who stood by their beliefs even when it came at a personal cost.

Some characters appear only briefly in the larger narrative, while others remain in the background despite playing an important role in shaping its events. Yet, their stories offer some of the most interesting perspectives on loyalty, devotion and duty.

Here are five such characters from the Ramayana who deserve their own moment in the spotlight.

1. Nishadraj Guha: The friend who stood by Ram when he needed him

Not every friendship in the Ramayana is shaped by royal status or power. Nishadraj Guha's bond with Lord Ram shows how genuine relationships go beyond social differences.

Guha, the king of the Nishad tribe (an indigenous and forest-dwelling community), meets Ram, Sita and Lakshman when they reach Shringaverpur during their exile. He doesn't see Ram as a prince who has lost his kingdom but welcomes him as a friend and offers him shelter and support.

At a time when Ram has been separated from his family and kingdom, Guha stands by him without expecting anything in return. Their bond also shows that Ram's relationships in the epic extend beyond kings, warriors and sages. His ability to connect with people across social boundaries is an important part of his character.

2. Ahalya: The woman waiting for redemption

One of the stories that deserved more space in Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana is that of Ahalya, the wife of sage Gautam. Often reduced to the tale of a woman cursed and later rescued by Ram, her story is far more layered. It brings up an uncomfortable question: why was Ahalya punished for an encounter in which she was deceived by Indra?

According to the epic, Indra, the king of the gods, approached Ahalya disguised as her husband while Gautam was away. When the sage learnt what had happened, he cursed Indra and Ahalya. While Indra faced the consequences of his deception, Ahalya was condemned to remain invisible in the hermitage, surviving on air and waiting for the day Ram would arrive.

The version most people are familiar with says that Gautam turned Ahalya into stone. When Ram's feet touched the stone, she was freed from the curse and came back to life. However, Valmiki's Ramayana tells it differently. Ahalya is not turned into stone; she becomes invisible to the world and continues to live in the hermitage, awaiting her redemption. Ram's arrival eventually brings an end to her punishment.

But there is more to Ahalya's story than Ram setting her free. Indra deceives her by taking on her husband's appearance, yet Ahalya is the one who is made to bear the consequences for years. Her story raises questions about blame, justice and the way women were judged in a society governed by the rules laid down by men.

Ahalya is often remembered as the woman Ram rescued. But perhaps her story deserves to be remembered for another reason: it makes us look at the injustice behind the curse, and at the woman who had to live with it.

3. Kevat: A boatman whose devotion became a story of its own

Kevat's part in the Ramayana is brief, but it has lived on through generations of retellings. A boatman by profession, he gets a moment with Ram, Sita and Lakshman during their exile that turns into one of the most remembered episodes in the epic.

As the three prepare to cross a river, Kevat is asked to take them across in his boat. But he has one condition before they can get in. He wants to wash Ram's feet first.

The reason behind his request is linked to the story of Ahalya, who was freed from a curse after Ram touched her with his feet. Kevat fears that if Ram's feet touch his wooden boat, it might also transform into something else. He therefore insists on washing them first.

What follows is a beautiful exchange between a devotee and the person he worships. Kevat is not interested in money or any reward for his service. For him, the opportunity to serve Ram is enough.

The episode is particularly popular in the Tulsiddas' Ramcharitmanas. Kevat's story also stands out because it gives an ordinary boatman a memorable place in an epic dominated by kings, princes and warriors. But, sadly this ordinary boatman went missing from the movie.

4. Urmila: The sacrifice that rarely gets its due

When people spoke about the sacrifices made during Ram's 14-year exile, Sita and Lakshman naturally came to mind. However, another character whose life changed just as dramatically because of their decision was Urmila.

The daughter of King Janaka and Sita's younger sister, Urmila was married to Lakshman. When Lakshman decided to accompany Ram into the forest, he left behind his wife and the life they could have shared in Ayodhya.

While Lakshman chose to serve his brother and sister-in-law, Urmila had to accept a separation that lasted 14 years. She remained in Ayodhya, away from her husband, as the events of the exile unfolded.

What made Urmila's story particularly moving was how little attention was often given to her perspective. Lakshman's commitment to Ram was celebrated as an example of brotherly devotion, but the personal cost of that decision for Urmila was not always explored.

Various retellings gave her a more prominent place, including stories that described her as making extraordinary sacrifices to support Lakshman's service during the exile. These details varied across versions of the epic.

Her story deserved to be told not simply as that of Lakshman's wife, but as that of a woman who had to find strength in a separation she had not chosen.

However, even Tiwari's Ramayana Part 1 did not do justice to her. Actor Sonia Balani played the role and was mostly seen in the background.

5. Mandodari: The queen who saw through Ravana's pride

Ravana was often remembered for his intelligence, strength, devotion to Lord Shiva and eventual downfall. But his wife, Mandodari, offered a different perspective on the events that led to Lanka's destruction. Actor Kajal Aggarwal portrayed her in Namit Malhotra's film.

The queen of Lanka was often portrayed as wise, composed and aware of the consequences of her husband's actions. Unlike those who supported Ravana out of fear or loyalty, Mandodari understood that his decision to abduct Sita would bring disaster upon their kingdom. However, in the Diwali release, Mandodari is a mera spectator of events unfolding in Lanka.

She repeatedly urged him to return Sita to Ram and avoid a war that could destroy everything he had built. Her advice did not stem from a lack of love for her husband. Rather, she understood the difference between personal pride and doing what was right. This we might get to see in Part 2.

Mandodari's position was particularly difficult as she was torn between her loyalty to Ravana and her understanding of his mistakes. She could see the consequences of his actions but could not change his decisions. Mandodari remained a voice of reason in a household increasingly consumed by ego and power and that was missing in the film.

The Ramayana is more than the story of its heroes

The enduring appeal of the Ramayana lies in the many stories within its larger narrative. Ram's journey remained at its centre, but the people he encountered, the relationships he built, and the choices made by those around him gave the epic its emotional depth.

Guha highlighted the value of friendship, while Kevat showed how devotion could be expressed through simple acts of service. Urmila's story brought attention to the sacrifices made away from the battlefield, and Mandodari represented the tragedy of wisdom going unheard. Ahalya's journey, meanwhile, explored themes of injustice, suffering and redemption.

As Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana introduced the epic to a new generation of cinema-goers, these characters offered plenty of possibilities for stories beyond the battles and core relationships. After all, an epic is not remembered only for its heroes. Sometimes, its most meaningful stories belong to those who stood beside them.

news.n_title: Move beyond stereotypical alpha male: Pankaj Tripathi on toxic masculinity in cinema
news.n_description: Pankaj Tripathi discussed redefining masculinity through his character in Parivarik ManuRanjan. He said varied portrayals could challenge patriarchal conditioning and conventional alpha male stereotypes.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Actor Pankaj Tripathi believes Indian cinema needs to broaden its understanding of masculinity, moving beyond the conventional portrayal of men as aggressive, dominant and physically intimidating. In an interview with India Today, the actor said there was a need to redefine what it means to be an alpha male, adding that masculinity can have several interpretations.

Speaking about his upcoming film Parivarik ManuRanjan, Tripathi reflected on how the film presents a different kind of male protagonist through his character, Ranjan Dubey. Asked whether cinema needs to rethink its portrayal of strong men, particularly at a time when aggressive and dominant male characters are increasingly visible on screen like in films like Animal and Toxic, the actor said, "Absolutely. There is a need to redefine it because there cannot be just one way of defining an alpha male or masculinity."

He added that audiences should be exposed to different representations of masculinity before forming their own understanding of it.

"There are several meanings and interpretations beyond that. When different perspectives reach the audience, they can decide which version of an alpha male they want to choose, or how they want to develop their own understanding of masculinity," he said.

Tripathi also pointed to the influence of patriarchal conditioning in shaping society's perception of men. "We have lived in a patriarchal society, and our conditioning over the years has been such that a particular image of a man has been created. That image gets transferred through even the smallest things," he said.

The actor said he hoped his character in Parivaarik Manoranjan would offer audiences another perspective. While actors sometimes portray characters whose beliefs may not necessarily align with their personal opinions, Tripathi said that if audiences wanted to understand his own sensibilities through his roles, Ranjan Dubey would be a good example.

Why Pankaj Tripathi said yes to Parivarik ManuRanjan

Explaining what drew him to the film, Tripathi said he was looking for a story that felt authentic rather than one that relied on the conventions of a particular genre.

"I don't choose films based on genres. I don't think that I have to do a romantic comedy now, followed by an action film and then a comedy. I need the right script," he said.

The actor revealed that he was drawn to the film's simple, slice-of-life storytelling and agreed to be part of it soon after reading the script.

"We have become accustomed to too much masala, both in entertainment and in life. This is comfort cinema. It is a simple story about two people from completely different worlds coming together in one courtyard. There are no unnecessary twists or turns. It is a sweet, simple story," he said.

Tripathi added that he felt Hindi cinema needed more such uncomplicated narratives, arguing that ordinary stories could be extraordinary in their own way.

Pankaj Tripathi on playing a character who defies stereotypes

One of the challenges of playing Ranjan Dubey, the actor explained, was preserving the character's innocence and humanity in his interactions with a woman who unexpectedly enters his home.

He said the film explores the possibility of two people of different genders sharing a space without their relationship necessarily being romantic or defined by conventional labels.

"Our habit is to assume that if two people of opposite genders are living together, there must be some relationship between them. We start imagining whether they are siblings or lovers. But two people of different genders can also simply coexist without any such relationship. The challenge was to ensure that his innocence and humanity remained intact," he said.

Tripathi also praised his co-star Aditi Rao Hydari, describing her as a sincere and hardworking performer. He recalled shooting the film in Lucknow during the peak of summer, adding that despite the extreme temperatures, the heat is not evident on screen.

The actor, who has frequently shot in Lucknow and Varanasi, said the two cities had become familiar destinations for him. Being from Bihar, a state neighbouring Uttar Pradesh, he particularly enjoys the food, conversations and people in the region.

With Parivaarik Manoranjan, Tripathi hopes audiences will encounter a different side of his acting. Asked whether the popularity of his iconic character Kaleen Bhaiya from Mirzapur could overshadow his quieter performances, he responded confidently: "Just let audiences watch the film on the 13th. They may not even remember Kaleen Bhaiya. People will wonder whether this is the same actor who plays Kaleen Bhaiya."

For Tripathi, however, the distinction between commercial success and artistic merit remains important. He said he does not pay much attention to the hit-or-flop conversation, arguing that box-office numbers are more relevant to the business of cinema than to its artistic value.

"Sometimes bad films make a lot of money, while some really wonderful films don't work at the box office. My job is to act honestly and do my work," he said.

Parivarik ManuRanjan is set to premiere on SonyLiv on November 13. Directed by Varun V Sharma, the film also features Aditi Rao Hydari, Sunita Rajwar, Brijendra Kala and Mukesh Tiwari.

news.n_title: Kimberly Powell: Jensen Huang's 2nd affair with Nvidia VP who is also married
news.n_description: Kimberly Powell joined Nvidia as a director in 2008 and has steadily risen through the company's ranks. According to her corporate profile, she initially worked on promoting the use of Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips in medical imaging.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Kimberly Powell has spent more than 18 years climbing the ranks at Nvidia, from joining the chipmaker as a director in 2008 to becoming its vice president of healthcare. Now, the 48-year-old executive has found herself in the spotlight for a very different reason: her alleged relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, 63, whom she reports to, according to a New York Times report.

The newspaper, citing five people who worked at Nvidia, reported that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel in San Jose, California, during the company's annual developer conference in March. Two of the sources said the interaction was captured on video.

The latest revelation comes amid a separate controversy surrounding Huang's affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials have linked to facilitating shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese companies.

Meanwhile, Huang, Powell, and Nvidia declined to comment on the matter.

WHO IS KIMBERLY POWELL?

Powell joined Nvidia as a director in 2008 and has steadily risen through the company's ranks. According to her corporate profile, she initially worked on promoting the use of Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips in medical imaging.

Before joining the chipmaker, Powell worked as an engineer and later in product development at an electronics startup. She eventually approached Nvidia to discuss its computing chips. When the company recognised the potential applications of its technology in healthcare, it contacted her about joining, she said in an episode of the Lifers podcast published in August.

Powell described the opportunity as a "dream come true" during the interview.

According to her LinkedIn profile, she was promoted to senior director in 2016 and led a business development team focused on artificial intelligence. By late 2017, she had become Nvidia's vice president of healthcare.

She currently oversees both the hardware and software sides of the company's healthcare business, including technology related to medical imaging, life sciences and drug discovery.

"I pretty much live and breathe healthcare. So I'm talking about it all the time," Powell told Business Insider in 2025.

According to a New York Post report, Powell's online activity indicates that she is married and has two children. However, her husband's identity is not known.

KIMBERLY POWELL'S ASSOCIATION WITH JENSEN HUANG

Having joined Nvidia in 2008, Powell has worked with Huang for over 18 years. The company's chief executive co-founded the chipmaker in 1993 and has led it ever since.

In her August interview with the Lifers podcast, Powell spoke about Huang's longstanding interest in healthcare and his ambitions for the sector.

"Jensen has been passionate about the healthcare industry going back 20-plus years, and that was really fuelled by seeing just researchers who had dreams and aspirations to do something very, very meaningful and impactful in the healthcare domain and us potentially having the tools to do it, to achieve that goal," she said.

The New York Times reported that Huang and Powell's alleged relationship had been discussed within Nvidia. It also cited two people who said the pair were seen being affectionate at a hotel during the company's March conference.

According to the newspaper, Huang's security personnel noticed a bystander recording the interaction and subsequently took the person aside. In another report published by the Times, which cited three people, the person was offered a non-disclosure agreement.

WHAT DOES NVIDIA'S CODE OF CONDUCT SAY?

The reports have also brought attention to Nvidia's workplace conduct policies. The company's code of conduct, which begins with a letter from Huang, identifies personal relationships as one of the activities that could create a conflict of interest.

It asks employees to avoid situations in which their actions create conflicts and states that the company "promptly investigates reports of misconduct."

NVIDIA PLANS TO OUST JENSEN HUANG AMID AFFAIR CONTROVERSY

The controversy surrounding Jensen Huang's personal relationships has put his position as Nvidia CEO under scrutiny. According to a Wall Street Journal report, the company's board is planning to remove the 63-year-old billionaire following revelations about his extramarital relationships.

The development comes amid reports that Nvidia is preparing to remove Huang as CEO, sending the company's shares down around 8 per cent in after-hours trading. Including Wednesday's sell-off, Nvidia has lost nearly USD 600 billion in market value this week. Bloomberg has also reported that the company's board is working with an outside firm to identify potential successors, as it lacks a clear succession plan.

The potential ouster of Huang, 63, could trigger significant leadership uncertainty at the nearly $4 trillion company, which he co-founded in 1993 and transformed into the world's leading supplier of artificial intelligence (AI) chips.

news.n_title: Pat Cummins caught on video in tense chat with wife in Sydney amid Sandpapergate row
news.n_description: Pat Cummins was spotted in an animated conversation with wife Becky in Sydney, marking his first public appearance since Usman Khawaja reignited the Sandpapergate controversy. The Australia captain is now preparing to address the allegations at a press conference.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Australia captain Pat Cummins was spotted having an animated conversation with his wife, Becky, on a Sydney street, in his first public appearance since Usman Khawaja's explosive claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. The footage has emerged as Cummins prepares to address the controversy surrounding Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr.

According to video published by The Australian on Wednesday, Cummins and Becky were seen engaged in a discussion before entering a nearby property. Dressed in a T-shirt and shorts, the Australian captain appeared relatively quiet during the exchange. He is currently resting from Australia's white-ball series against England ahead of their upcoming four-Test series against New Zealand.

Cummins had earlier maintained that the 2018 scandal had been investigated thoroughly and that the Australian team had moved on from the episode.

"It's obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times," Cummins had said.

"It was dealt with then, all I can say is as a group we've moved on. Very happy with the last eight or nine years, how we've been as a group and evolved. He didn't go into too much detail... As always it was 'no worries, you can tell your story, that's fine'."

Khawaja's autobiography has reopened the debate over the Cape Town Test of 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper to alter the ball. Cricket Australia subsequently suspended Bancroft, David Warner and Steve Smith, with the latter two also losing leadership positions.

KHAWAJA PUTS BOWLING GROUP UNDER SPOTLIGHT

Khawaja has alleged that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan extended across the Australian dressing room and coaching staff, and that the practice had begun during the previous Test in Port Elizabeth. He has also questioned why the investigation did not interview him, despite him being part of the touring squad.

Warner has backed Khawaja's account, describing his claims as accurate. Mitchell Starc, however, has stood by the bowling group's earlier position that they were unaware of sandpaper being taken onto the field.

Cummins has now called a press conference at Cricket Central in Sydney for Friday morning, offering to answer questions about the allegations. He said he had taken time to understand the full extent of Khawaja's claims before responding.

The appearance will put the Australia captain under renewed scrutiny, particularly over what the bowling group knew about the events in South Africa and the joint statement issued by the quartet in 2021.

news.n_title: Nvidia's next boss? Who could replace Jensen Huang as his job hangs in the balance
news.n_description: While Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress and vice-president Ian Buck seem to be top contenders, eight executives outside the chip-making giant are emerging as potential names to watch if the chipmaker has to find a replacement for its long-time leader.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Nvidia's search for a possible successor to Jensen Huang could extend well beyond the company's own leadership team. While Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress and vice-president Ian Buck seem to be top contenders, eight executives outside the chip-making giant are emerging as potential names to watch if the chipmaker has to find a replacement for its long-time leader.

According to a Bloomberg report, Nvidia has tapped an outside firm to identify potential candidates following reports of multiple extramarital relationships involving Huang. The search could prove challenging for the world's most valuable chipmaker, given how closely its strategy, technology direction and business relationships have been shaped by its co-founder.

Among the eight names identified by Bloomberg are executives from Nvidia, Arm, AMD, Apple, Amazon and Google. Buck and Kress are two of the most prominent internal names, while the list also includes leaders who run major technology and semiconductor businesses outside Nvidia.

Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to discuss Huang's future, but has not announced any decision regarding the company's longtime CEO, reported The New York Times.

The development comes amid growing uncertainty over Huang's future. Nvidia's board is examining the controversy surrounding the CEO, while investors are also weighing the potential consequences of losing a leader who has run the company since co-founding it in 1993.

WHO ARE THE EIGHT POTENTIAL SUCCESSORS?

Colette Kress: Nvidia's CFO and possible interim leader

Kress is Nvidia's executive vice-president and chief financial officer. She joined the company in September 2013 and is among its best-known executives after Huang, particularly among investors.

Before joining Nvidia, she spent three years as senior vice-president and CFO of Cisco's Business Technology and Operations Finance organisation. She also spent 13 years at Microsoft, including four years as CFO of its Server and Tools division. Earlier in her career, she held finance roles at Texas Instruments.

Her experience managing the finances of large technology companies could make her a possible choice to steady Nvidia during a leadership transition. However, finance chiefs are often viewed as interim leaders rather than long-term replacements, particularly at technology companies.

Bloomberg has separately reported that Kress could take over as interim CEO and oversee the search for a permanent successor if Huang exits.

Ian Buck: The Nvidia executive behind CUDA

Buck is a vice-president at Nvidia who oversees products for data centres, including the company's AI chips. He is also the inventor of CUDA, the software framework that helps developers use Nvidia's chips for AI and other computing applications.

His technical expertise and familiarity with Nvidia's customers make him an important internal candidate. He is also a familiar face to the company's data centre customers.

However, Bloomberg noted that Buck lacks the operational experience that investors often look for in the head of a large publicly listed company.

In a separate Bloomberg report on prediction markets, Buck emerged as the favourite to replace Huang on Kalshi and Polymarket, attracting around a third of bets on both platforms. Kress ranked second. These rankings reflect market expectations, not an official Nvidia shortlist.

Rene Haas: The former Nvidia executive now leading Arm

Haas is the chief executive of Arm Holdings, a major chip-design company with a close partnership with Nvidia.

He previously worked at Nvidia and now manages a complex network of customers and partners, giving him insight into the semiconductor industry and the wider technology market.

Nvidia itself attempted to acquire Arm in 2020 in a deal involving SoftBank, but the transaction eventually collapsed after facing antitrust scrutiny.

His experience running a major chip-design business and his familiarity with Nvidia could make him a potential name in the search.

Lisa Su: The leader of Nvidia's closest rival

Su is the chief executive of Advanced Micro Devices, Nvidia's closest competitor in the market for AI chips and high-performance computing.

Under her leadership, AMD has strengthened its position in the semiconductor industry and overtaken Intel in several areas of technological leadership. Its shares have also surged nearly 170-fold during her tenure, according to Bloomberg.

Su brings extensive experience in chip engineering and running a large semiconductor company. However, AMD remains considerably smaller than Nvidia, and its AI chips have yet to match Nvidia's level of adoption.

Her inclusion would be notable given that she currently leads one of Nvidia's biggest competitors.

Johny Srouji: The man behind Apple's custom chips

Srouji is Apple's chief hardware officer and has led the company's in-house silicon programme.

He has overseen the development of custom chips used in the iPhone, Mac and other Apple devices. His experience gives him strong credentials in chip design, product integration and long-term technology planning.

However, Bloomberg noted that much of his experience has been built within Apple's tightly controlled business structure. He has also not been tested in the kind of high-profile salesmanship and public-facing role that Huang has built at Nvidia.

Matt Garman: The Amazon executive running AWS

Garman is the chief executive of Amazon Web Services, the cloud-computing business of Amazon.

He oversees a large operation that rents computing power through an extensive network of data centres and also develops Amazon's own chips.

Like Huang, Garman combines technical and operational experience. His leadership of a major cloud-computing business could be relevant to Nvidia, given the importance of data centres and AI infrastructure to its growth.

One challenge highlighted by Bloomberg is that Amazon was initially seen as lagging competitors such as Microsoft and Google in building AI infrastructure.

Sanjay Mehrotra: The Micron chief with semiconductor experience

Mehrotra is the chief executive of Micron Technology, one of the world's leading memory chipmakers.

He has experience steering a semiconductor company through industry cycles, including periods of weak demand and strong growth. Micron's shares have risen more than 2,700% during his tenure, helped by increasing demand for memory chips amid the AI boom, according to Bloomberg.

However, his experience is rooted largely in memory chips and manufacturing, rather than graphics processing units and the software ecosystem that has helped Nvidia dominate AI computing.

Amin Vahdat: Google's AI chip specialist

Vahdat oversees Google's tensor processing unit programme, which develops the company's in-house AI chips.

His technical credentials are significant, particularly as Google builds alternatives to Nvidia's GPUs for AI workloads.

However, Bloomberg noted that he has less experience running a large publicly listed company with Nvidia's scale, commercial complexity and investor scrutiny.

WHAT ABOUT JENSEN HUANG'S FAMILY?

Three members of Huang's family also work at Nvidia: his children Madison and Spencer, and his son-in-law Nico Caprez.

Madison oversees product and technical marketing, while Spencer works in product management in Nvidia's robotics division. Caprez holds the more prominent position among the three as vice-president of global AI infrastructure growth and is involved in discussions with emerging cloud companies and data centre deployments.

Huang has previously said he does not wish the burden of running Nvidia on his children. He has also said that if they aspire to lead the company, they would have to earn the position.

Their presence at Nvidia is part of the wider succession discussion, but Bloomberg's list of eight potential candidates does not identify them as formal contenders.

WHY REPLACING JENSEN HUANG WILL BE DIFFICULT

Huang has led Nvidia since co-founding it in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. Over more than three decades, he has helped transform the company from a graphics-card maker into a dominant supplier of chips and technology used in artificial intelligence.

His role extends beyond product development. He has shaped Nvidia's relationships with customers, suppliers, partners and start-ups, while also playing a prominent part in promoting the wider AI industry.

Bloomberg has highlighted how central Huang remains to the company's daily operations. Around 60 senior executives report directly to him, and major decisions continue to flow through the CEO.

This creates what is known as key-person risk: the possibility that a company depends too heavily on one individual.

The challenge for Nvidia is therefore not just finding someone with semiconductor expertise. The next CEO would need to combine technical understanding, operational experience, investor confidence and the ability to maintain relationships across a vast AI ecosystem.

For a company that has been shaped by one leader for more than three decades, finding someone who can take on that role may be one of its most consequential decisions.

news.n_title: How Rajiv Gandhi introduced Sonia to Satyajit Ray's films and Mohammed Rafi's ghazals
news.n_description: In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi recalls how Rajiv Gandhi introduced her to Indian music, cinema and photography in London.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Rajiv Gandhi introduced Sonia Gandhi to several aspects of Indian culture long before she became part of the Gandhi family. From Mohammed Rafi's ghazals and Ravi Shankar's sitar to Satyajit Ray's celebrated films, their time together in London gave her a window into a country that would eventually become her home.

In her autobiography, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi recalls Rajiv's interests beyond academics and his love for photography, music and cinema. Photography, she writes, was a hobby he had picked up from his father. In his free time, the two would visit the Imperial laboratory, where Rajiv developed his own photographs of Sonia, their friends and nature.

Music was another passion. Rajiv would save up to buy records for himself, his mother and friends. The couple occasionally visited the HMV record shop in London, where they would spend hours listening to music before exercising restraint and buying just one record each.

His musical tastes were varied, spanning jazz and pop as well as Western and Indian classical music. He also introduced Sonia to jazz and different genres of Indian music. Among his gifts to her were a record of ghazals by Mohammed Rafi and another featuring sitar maestro Ravi Shankar.

Cinema was another way Rajiv introduced Sonia to Indian culture. He took her to watch the Merchant Ivory Productions’ film Shakespeare Wallah and Satyajit Ray's acclaimed Apu Trilogy.

“He'd taken me to watch the Merchant and Ivory film Shakespeare Wallah and Satyajit Ray's trilogy, Pather Panchali, Aparajito, and Apur Sansar, opening up for me a small window on different shades of Indian life,” she writes.

If anything, Belonging: A Journey of Love offers readers a glimpse into Sonia Gandhi's life beyond politics, revealing the person behind the public persona and offering a more intimate account of her life and experiences.

The book was launched on November 10 and is available to purchase on Blinkit and Amazon.

news.n_title: Govt employees can now get laptops worth up to Rs 1.8 lakh, keep them after 4 years
news.n_description: Central government officers can now get laptops worth up to Rs 1.8 lakh and retain them after four years under the Finance Ministry's revised device purchase rules. Here are all the details.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Government employees could soon be taking home the laptops they use for office work, without having to pay for them. The Finance Ministry has revised its device purchase policy, allowing eligible central government officers to keep their government-issued laptops, tablets and similar gadgets after four years of use. According to ANI, the new rules also allow departments to buy devices costing up to Rs 1.8 lakh plus taxes. In this range, one can get MacBook Air and Pro models from Apple.

The higher price limit, however, comes with a condition. A device must have more than 40 per cent Make-in-India (MII) content to qualify for the Rs 1.8 lakh ceiling. For other devices, the maximum permitted cost is Rs 1.5 lakh plus taxes. Both limits include standard software. The revised policy was issued by the Department of Expenditure on November 10. It replaces the earlier rules from July 2023, when the government had set the corresponding price limits at Rs 1 lakh and Rs 1.3 lakh.

The policy allows ministries and departments to issue laptops, tablets, notepads, ultrabooks, notebooks and similar devices to officers for official work. Mobile phones, which were specifically mentioned in the earlier guidelines, do not feature in the new list.

Which government employees will get the devices?

Not every government employee will automatically qualify for a new laptop. Officers in Pay Level 12 and above are eligible, covering the entire sanctioned strength at these levels. For employees in Pay Levels 8 to 11, the initial eligibility is restricted to half the sanctioned posts. This can be increased to 75 per cent if the ministry or department secretary, in consultation with the Financial Adviser, considers it necessary for official work.

There are also conditions attached to keeping the devices. Officers can retain their laptops after four years, but departments must first wipe all official information stored on them. Those who retire or leave government service before completing four years will not necessarily have to return their devices. They can keep them by paying the depreciated value, with the government calculating depreciation at 25 per cent annually.

The rules also prevent an officer from receiving another device within the four-year period unless the existing one is found to be beyond economical repair. The revised policy applies to central government ministries and departments, along with their attached and subordinate offices. State governments, public sector undertakings, autonomous bodies and consultants are outside its scope.
