news.n_title: 25 kg gold stolen from Tanishq showroom in Madurai 15 days after opening
news.n_description: Three masked burglars broke into a newly opened Tanishq showroom in Madurai and stole around 30 per cent of its gold stock.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Masked burglars broke into a newly opened Tanishq jewellery showroom in Madurai and fled with gold ornaments worth several crores of rupees, news agency Press Trust of India reported, quoting police officials.

While the police have not yet confirmed the exact value of the stolen jewellery, local media reports estimated that around 20-25 kg of gold, worth more than Rs 30 crore, may have been stolen. Some reports have put the estimated value significantly higher. However, neither the police nor the showroom management has confirmed these figures so far.

The theft came to light on Thursday morning when employees arrived to open the showroom on Madurai Bypass Road. The outlet had been inaugurated just 15 days ago, ahead of Diwali.

Preliminary investigations suggest that the burglars gained entry by breaking through the rear wall and doors of the showroom. Madurai City Commissioner of Police S Rajendran inspected the crime scene along with Deputy Commissioners of Police AG Inigo Divyan and S Vanitha.

Rajendran said CCTV footage indicated that three people were involved in the burglary.

"Three persons broke the wall and door to enter the shop. About 30 per cent of the total goods in the shop has been stolen. An investigation is underway to determine the exact value of the stolen jewellery," he told reporters, according to PTI.

Sniffer dogs were deployed at the scene, while investigators began examining CCTV footage from the surrounding areas to identify and trace the suspects.

Divyan said the burglars had taken only jewellery displayed in the showroom, leaving ornaments stored in lockers untouched. He added that the exact value of the stolen gold would be established only after the showroom management filed a formal complaint.

"We cannot state anything based on assumptions right now," he said.

Police have formed special investigation teams under three Assistant Commissioners of Police. Each team comprises three inspectors. The teams are examining CCTV footage and gathering evidence to identify the three suspects and establish the exact quantity and value of the stolen jewellery.

news.n_title: BJP leader gifts bikes to 4 party workers, son promises Scorpio if father wins polls
news.n_description: Rajpal Singh Chauhan gifted motorcycles to four BJP mandal presidents at a Diwali programme. His son's SUV promise has fuelled political discussion ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
A Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader in Uttar Pradesh's Moradabad has triggered political discussion after gifting motorcycles to four mandal presidents in the Thakurdwara Assembly constituency on Diwali.

The leader's son has also promised to give each of them a Scorpio SUV if his father wins the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

Rajpal Singh Chauhan, a former BJP district president who has contested the Thakurdwara Assembly seat twice, presented the motorcycles to the four mandal presidents during a workers' conference and Diwali Milan programme organised in the constituency. His son, Amit Chauhan, made the announcement about the proposed Scorpio gifts during the event.

The four mandal presidents who received motorcycles are Deepak Valmiki, Hariom Singh Chauhan, Harpal Singh Saini and Pawan Kumar Sharma. They were invited on stage and honoured before being handed the keys to their new vehicles. Former party office-bearers were also given gifts at the programme, which was attended by several BJP leaders and workers.

BJP LEADER'S SON PROMISES FOUR SCORPIO SUVS

The announcement that attracted particular attention was Amit Chauhan's promise to gift a Scorpio to each of the four mandal presidents if his father becomes an MLA in 2027.

While the motorcycles were presented during the Diwali event, the four SUVs were promised in the event of Rajpal Singh Chauhan's electoral victory. The announcement has since become a talking point in Thakurdwara's political circles, particularly as parties begin preparing for the 2027 Assembly elections.

RAJPAL SINGH CHAUHAN EYES THIRD ATTEMPT IN 2027

Rajpal Singh Chauhan has previously contested the Thakurdwara Assembly seat twice on a BJP ticket but failed to win either election. His recent organisational activities and outreach to party workers have brought attention to his political ambitions ahead of the next Assembly polls.

The Thakurdwara seat is expected to see competition among several BJP leaders seeking the party's nomination. However, the party has not announced its candidate for the constituency.

The role of mandal presidents is considered important in the BJP's organisational structure, as they coordinate party activities at the local level and help mobilise workers during elections. They also play a role in connecting booth-level workers with the party leadership.

BJP DISTRICT PRESIDENT DISTANCES PARTY FROM GIFTS

Reacting to the development, BJP district president Akash Pal said that gifting something to a party worker or office-bearer on Diwali was a personal matter and had no connection with the organisation.

He said he had spoken to all four mandal presidents over the phone and advised them to maintain the dignity of the organisation and discharge their responsibilities impartially.

RAJPAL SINGH CHAUHAN CHALLENGES AKHILESH YADAV

During the Diwali Milan programme, Rajpal Singh Chauhan also targeted Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and challenged him to contest the 2027 Assembly elections from Thakurdwara.

Chauhan claimed that if Yadav contested from the constituency, the BJP would ensure that he lost his security deposit. He also made remarks about the Ayodhya and Lord Ram issues and advised the SP chief to visit Vrindavan.

With the 2027 Assembly elections approaching, the motorcycle gifts and the promise of Scorpio SUVs have added another dimension to the political activity in Thakurdwara.

news.n_title: Divorce allowed in foreign country cannot end marriage in India: Supreme Court
news.n_description: The court held that a foreign divorce decree must meet the conditions prescribed under Section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) before it can be recognised by Indian courts.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
The Supreme Court has observed that a marriage solemnised in India cannot be automatically dissolved or stand null and void by a divorce order passed by a foreign court, reiterating that such judgments must satisfy the requirements of Indian law to be legally recognised in the country.

The top court also specifically held that a foreign divorce granted solely on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage cannot be treated as valid in India when the marriage was solemnised under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

A bench comprising Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar made the observation on Tuesday while dismissing a man's plea seeking quashing of criminal proceedings initiated against him for bigamy and criminal conspiracy.

The court held that a foreign divorce decree must meet the conditions prescribed under Section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) before it can be recognised by Indian courts.

"In our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily," the bench observed.

It further stated that the decree violated the legal requirements under Section 13 of the CPC, which every foreign judgment must satisfy to be enforceable in India.

The court emphasised that the validity of a marriage solemnised under Indian law cannot be determined solely on the basis of proceedings conducted in a foreign jurisdiction.

It also rejected the argument that the husband's subsequent foreign citizenship and divorce proceedings abroad could absolve him of liability under Indian law.

"We cannot accept this submission in the manner canvassed as accused No.1/husband was married to respondent No.2/first wife in India under the Hindu rites, rituals and customs," the bench said.

The court added that even if the second marriage took place outside India, the allegations under Section 494 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) could not be diluted, as an inquiry into bigamy must consider whether the first marriage continued to subsist.

The case concerned a man who married his first wife on April 18, 2003, in Sattenapalli, Andhra Pradesh, according to Hindu rites and customs.

The couple subsequently lived in Hyderabad, where the husband was pursuing his postgraduate studies at Osmania Medical College.

On February 4, 2005, the husband moved to the United Kingdom to pursue a career as a doctor, and his wife joined him later.

In August 2007, she returned to her parental home in Sattenapalli for childbirth. The husband subsequently claimed that she did not return to the UK despite his repeated requests.

As their matrimonial relationship deteriorated, the husband initiated divorce and child custody proceedings before a competent court in Narasaraopet, Guntur district.

However, the proceedings were dismissed. He later approached the Andhra Pradesh High Court but withdrew the appeal.

The husband acquired British citizenship on February 1, 2013, and subsequently approached the Cambridge County Court in England for divorce.

In 2014, the foreign court granted him a divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage. He later married another woman in Norfolk, UK.

Nearly two years after the second marriage, his first wife lodged a complaint at the Sattenapalli town police station, alleging offences under Sections 494 and 120B read with Section 34 of the IPC.

The Supreme Court refused to quash the criminal proceedings against the husband, while setting aside the proceedings against his parents and second wife.

The ruling reiterates that foreign divorce decrees involving marriages solemnised in India cannot automatically alter marital status under Indian law.

Such decrees must satisfy the statutory requirements, including recognised grounds for divorce, proper jurisdiction, principles of natural justice and absence of fraud.

Consequently, a person who remarries on the strength of a foreign divorce decree that is not recognised in India may still face prosecution for bigamy.

news.n_title: Jailer 2 on OTT: No deleted Mohanlal, Santhanam's scenes in streaming version

news.n_title: Ramayana Part 2: 60 per cent filmed, here's what remains before 2028 release
news.n_description: Cinematographer Pankaj Kumar revealed that 60 per cent of Ramayana Part 2 has been shot. He also shared why the sequel will be bigger than the first film.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Cinematographer Pankaj Kumar has revealed that about 60 per cent of Ramayana Part 2 has been shot. However, extensive visual effects and motion-capture work remains as director Nitesh Tiwari and his team prepare to bring Hanuman, the vanar sena and the epic’s major battles to the screen.

The sequel, featuring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, is planned on a larger scale than the first instalment. Initially expected to release in 2027, the film has been pushed to 2028 to give the team more time to complete its technical and post-production work.

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter India, Kumar said that although a significant portion of the sequel had been filmed, considerable work was still pending.

“We have already shot about 60 per cent of Part 2. A lot of VFX work, a lot of motion-capture work is left because the second part is going to be more grand than the first part. It has a lot more CG characters, like Hanuman and the whole vanar sena. A lot more details need to be worked on,” he said.

The second instalment will require detailed computer-generated imagery for Lord Hanuman and the vanar sena. Motion capture will also be used to place the characters convincingly within the film’s fantasy setting. The team will have to create an army of digital characters while maintaining visual consistency across the film.

Why the forests have a fantastical look

The visual treatment of Ramayana, including its forests, trees and natural surroundings, has drawn attention for its fantastical appearance. Kumar said the team had never intended to recreate a real forest. Instead, it wanted to build an enhanced world suited to the scale and imagination of the epic.

“See, if we shot Ramayana in a real jungle, the world would look very real, but maybe that’s not what we’re looking for. We want our world to look more enhanced, better than the real forest. For the forests that Ram and Lakshman are walking in to fight demons, realistic trees in the jungle may not give us that larger-than-life experience, with giant monsters attacking and our characters swinging from one tree to the other. Where is realism in that? There is no realism in that. You are giving a fantasy world to the audience. So why be a stickler for realistic-looking leaves or branches? It’s just a different medium of expressing yourself,” he said.

The approach is intended to give the story’s demons, divine powers and large battles a distinct visual language rather than recreate everyday landscapes.

Release pushed to 2028

Ramayana was planned as a two-part cinematic adaptation, with the second instalment initially expected in 2027. Producer Namit Malhotra has since confirmed that it will now arrive in 2028.

Explaining the delay in an interview with E! News, Malhotra said, “That extra year is what I genuinely believe we need to do justice for a film of this size.”

The additional time will allow the team to work on the sequel’s extensive visual effects and other technical requirements. Its larger scale and greater number of computer-generated characters will make post-production particularly demanding.

The cast of Ramayana

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Part One stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Ravie Dubey plays Lakshman, while Sunny Deol portrays Lord Hanuman.

The supporting cast includes Arun Govil as King Dasharatha, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi, Indira Krishnan as Kaushalya, Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari and Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha.

Vivek Oberoi plays Vidyutjihva, Faisal Malik essays the role of Kumbhkarna, Harish Uthaman portrays Vibhishana and Kunal Kapoor plays Lord Indra. Anupam Kher lends his voice to Jatayu.

The sequel is expected to explore the events leading to the battle between Rama and Ravana. Meghnad, also known as Indrajit and the son of Ravana, will have a significant role. Raghav Juyal has been cast as the character, whose appearance was revealed in a post-credit scene in the first instalment.

news.n_title: Ramayana beyond Rama and Sita: 5 fascinating characters who deserve bigger spotlight
news.n_description: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana renews attention on Guha, Kevat, Urmila, Mandodari and Vibhishan. Their stories deepen the epic's exploration of friendship, devotion, sacrifice, wisdom and righteousness.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
With Ramayana: Rise of a Legend Nitesh Tiwari has brought one of India's most celebrated epics to the big screen with larger-than-life visuals, grand sequences and characters that have lived in our collective memory for generations. While Lord Rama, Goddess Sita, Lakshman and Ravana remain central to the story, the epic is also shaped by several other characters whose contributions deserve equal attention.

The Ramayana is not just the story of Ram's journey to Lanka, his battle with Ravana and his return to Ayodhya. It is also a story of friendships that crossed social boundaries, sacrifices that went unnoticed, difficult moral choices and people who stood by their beliefs even when it came at a personal cost.

Some characters appear only briefly in the larger narrative, while others remain in the background despite playing an important role in shaping its events. Yet, their stories offer some of the most interesting perspectives on loyalty, devotion and duty.

Here are five such characters from the Ramayana who deserve their own moment in the spotlight.

1. Nishadraj Guha: The friend who stood by Ram when he needed him

Not every friendship in the Ramayana is shaped by royal status or power. Nishadraj Guha's bond with Lord Ram shows how genuine relationships go beyond social differences.

Guha, the king of the Nishad tribe (an indigenous and forest-dwelling community), meets Ram, Sita and Lakshman when they reach Shringaverpur during their exile. He doesn't see Ram as a prince who has lost his kingdom but welcomes him as a friend and offers him shelter and support.

At a time when Ram has been separated from his family and kingdom, Guha stands by him without expecting anything in return. Their bond also shows that Ram's relationships in the epic extend beyond kings, warriors and sages. His ability to connect with people across social boundaries is an important part of his character.

2. Ahalya: The woman waiting for redemption

One of the stories that deserved more space in Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana is that of Ahalya, the wife of sage Gautam. Often reduced to the tale of a woman cursed and later rescued by Ram, her story is far more layered. It brings up an uncomfortable question: why was Ahalya punished for an encounter in which she was deceived by Indra?

According to the epic, Indra, the king of the gods, approached Ahalya disguised as her husband while Gautam was away. When the sage learnt what had happened, he cursed Indra and Ahalya. While Indra faced the consequences of his deception, Ahalya was condemned to remain invisible in the hermitage, surviving on air and waiting for the day Ram would arrive.

The version most people are familiar with says that Gautam turned Ahalya into stone. When Ram's feet touched the stone, she was freed from the curse and came back to life. However, Valmiki's Ramayana tells it differently. Ahalya is not turned into stone; she becomes invisible to the world and continues to live in the hermitage, awaiting her redemption. Ram's arrival eventually brings an end to her punishment.

But there is more to Ahalya's story than Ram setting her free. Indra deceives her by taking on her husband's appearance, yet Ahalya is the one who is made to bear the consequences for years. Her story raises questions about blame, justice and the way women were judged in a society governed by the rules laid down by men.

Ahalya is often remembered as the woman Ram rescued. But perhaps her story deserves to be remembered for another reason: it makes us look at the injustice behind the curse, and at the woman who had to live with it.

3. Kevat: A boatman whose devotion became a story of its own

Kevat's part in the Ramayana is brief, but it has lived on through generations of retellings. A boatman by profession, he gets a moment with Ram, Sita and Lakshman during their exile that turns into one of the most remembered episodes in the epic.

As the three prepare to cross a river, Kevat is asked to take them across in his boat. But he has one condition before they can get in. He wants to wash Ram's feet first.

The reason behind his request is linked to the story of Ahalya, who was freed from a curse after Ram touched her with his feet. Kevat fears that if Ram's feet touch his wooden boat, it might also transform into something else. He therefore insists on washing them first.

What follows is a beautiful exchange between a devotee and the person he worships. Kevat is not interested in money or any reward for his service. For him, the opportunity to serve Ram is enough.

The episode is particularly popular in the Tulsiddas' Ramcharitmanas. Kevat's story also stands out because it gives an ordinary boatman a memorable place in an epic dominated by kings, princes and warriors. But, sadly this ordinary boatman went missing from the movie.

4. Urmila: The sacrifice that rarely gets its due

When people spoke about the sacrifices made during Ram's 14-year exile, Sita and Lakshman naturally came to mind. However, another character whose life changed just as dramatically because of their decision was Urmila.

The daughter of King Janaka and Sita's younger sister, Urmila was married to Lakshman. When Lakshman decided to accompany Ram into the forest, he left behind his wife and the life they could have shared in Ayodhya.

While Lakshman chose to serve his brother and sister-in-law, Urmila had to accept a separation that lasted 14 years. She remained in Ayodhya, away from her husband, as the events of the exile unfolded.

What made Urmila's story particularly moving was how little attention was often given to her perspective. Lakshman's commitment to Ram was celebrated as an example of brotherly devotion, but the personal cost of that decision for Urmila was not always explored.

Various retellings gave her a more prominent place, including stories that described her as making extraordinary sacrifices to support Lakshman's service during the exile. These details varied across versions of the epic.

Her story deserved to be told not simply as that of Lakshman's wife, but as that of a woman who had to find strength in a separation she had not chosen.

However, even Tiwari's Ramayana Part 1 did not do justice to her. Actor Sonia Balani played the role and was mostly seen in the background.

5. Mandodari: The queen who saw through Ravana's pride

Ravana was often remembered for his intelligence, strength, devotion to Lord Shiva and eventual downfall. But his wife, Mandodari, offered a different perspective on the events that led to Lanka's destruction. Actor Kajal Aggarwal portrayed her in Namit Malhotra's film.

The queen of Lanka was often portrayed as wise, composed and aware of the consequences of her husband's actions. Unlike those who supported Ravana out of fear or loyalty, Mandodari understood that his decision to abduct Sita would bring disaster upon their kingdom. However, in the Diwali release, Mandodari is a mera spectator of events unfolding in Lanka.

She repeatedly urged him to return Sita to Ram and avoid a war that could destroy everything he had built. Her advice did not stem from a lack of love for her husband. Rather, she understood the difference between personal pride and doing what was right. This we might get to see in Part 2.

Mandodari's position was particularly difficult as she was torn between her loyalty to Ravana and her understanding of his mistakes. She could see the consequences of his actions but could not change his decisions. Mandodari remained a voice of reason in a household increasingly consumed by ego and power and that was missing in the film.

The Ramayana is more than the story of its heroes

The enduring appeal of the Ramayana lies in the many stories within its larger narrative. Ram's journey remained at its centre, but the people he encountered, the relationships he built, and the choices made by those around him gave the epic its emotional depth.

Guha highlighted the value of friendship, while Kevat showed how devotion could be expressed through simple acts of service. Urmila's story brought attention to the sacrifices made away from the battlefield, and Mandodari represented the tragedy of wisdom going unheard. Ahalya's journey, meanwhile, explored themes of injustice, suffering and redemption.

As Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana introduced the epic to a new generation of cinema-goers, these characters offered plenty of possibilities for stories beyond the battles and core relationships. After all, an epic is not remembered only for its heroes. Sometimes, its most meaningful stories belong to those who stood beside them.

news.n_title: What Sonia Gandhi says and doesn't say about the Bachchan family in her book
news.n_description: Sonia Gandhi recalls how Teji and Harivansh Rai Bachchan welcomed and guided her in India. Her memoir celebrates that early warmth while leaving the families' later estrangement largely unexplained.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, takes readers back to a time when the Gandhi and Bachchan families shared a close personal bond. Long before Amitabh Bachchan became one of India's biggest film stars and Sonia Gandhi entered politics, the two families were connected through friendship, affection and years of shared history.

Interestingly, some of Sonia's warmest recollections in the book are not about Amitabh himself but his parents, poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan and his wife, Teji Bachchan. She remembers them as the people who helped her find her feet in India when she arrived from Italy in January 1968 to marry Rajiv Gandhi.

At the time, Sonia was a young woman entering an unfamiliar country, struggling with the language, customs and expectations of a new family. It was Indira Gandhi who arranged for her to stay with the Bachchans at their Delhi residence, 13 Willingdon Crescent, before her wedding.

The Bachchans were old family friends of the Nehru-Gandhis from Allahabad. Their home became Sonia's first place of comfort in India. Amitabh Bachchan, who was already friends with Rajiv, was also among those who welcomed her when she arrived at the airport.

Sonia remembers Teji Bachchan with particular affection. She describes her as a maternal figure who helped her understand Indian customs and made her feel at home. Teji looked after her when she fell ill and remained attentive to her needs. The relationship went beyond the initial hospitality. Sonia also recalls receiving gifts from her over the years, including a puppy after the death of her firstborn son, who lived for only a few hours.

In her memoir, Sonia describes Teji as someone who was always willing to help and guide her. Harivansh Rai Bachchan, meanwhile, helped her with Hindi and offered advice that stayed with her long after those early days.

Recalling her arrival in Delhi, Sonia writes: "Tiny Mrs. Bachchan, clad in a jacket and slacks, head covered in a French-style scarf, welcomed me in the porch with the sweetest of smiles and a warm embrace. I felt at once relieved and reassured."

She also remembers how Harivansh Rai Bachchan would occasionally teach her Hindi. Despite having studied English for years, she found it difficult to communicate fluently and understand Indian accents. The poet would use their brief conversations to offer her advice about navigating life in India.

One particular observation stayed with her: "You must know, Sonia beti, child, that in this country it is not what you are that counts, it is what people think you to be."

At the time, the young Sonia struggled to understand what he meant. She wondered whether his advice meant she could never truly be herself. She admits that she would often cry quietly on her way home after being dropped back by Rajiv, missing her family and the life she had left behind in Italy.

Looking back, however, she understood the wisdom in his words. In the book, she writes:

"This warning invariably left me wondering—does he mean that I can never be myself? I was I, and that's the way I was; how could I possibly show myself differently? So it was that on many occasions, after being dropped back by Rajiv, I'd shed some quiet tears and long for my home and my family. Rajiv tried to reassure me. But in later years I remembered Uncle Bachchan's words. How right he'd been - a poet and a sensitive man, having himself experienced the fickleness of the public."

From family friends to a relationship that turned distant

The warmth of these memories becomes particularly interesting when placed against the later history of the two families.

Amitabh Bachchan and Rajiv Gandhi's friendship went back to their childhood. Their families had known each other for decades, with the connection beginning in Allahabad through Harivansh Rai Bachchan's friendship with the Nehru family. The two boys grew up around each other and remained close as adults.

Rajiv was also present during some of Amitabh's most difficult moments. When the actor met with a near-fatal accident while shooting Coolie in 1982, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv were among those who stood by the Bachchan family.

Amitabh eventually entered politics in 1984, contesting the Lok Sabha election from Allahabad as a Congress candidate. He won by a massive margin, defeating former Uttar Pradesh chief minister HN Bahuguna.

However, his political journey did not last long. The Bofors controversy, which erupted in 1987 over allegations of kickbacks in the purchase of Swedish artillery guns, brought considerable political pressure on the Congress government led by Rajiv. Amitabh's name also became embroiled in the controversy, although he denied any wrongdoing. He resigned from Parliament in 1987 and later fought legal battles to clear his name.

The relationship between the two families reportedly became strained over the years. The reasons have been discussed in various accounts, with disagreements, political developments and personal differences all featuring in the history of their falling out. The distance became more apparent after Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.

There were also public indications of the strained relationship in later years. In 2004, Amitabh's wife Jaya Bachchan, by then associated with the Samajwadi Party, and Rahul Gandhi were involved in a public exchange of remarks over the relationship between the two families.

Despite this complicated history, Sonia's memoir does not dwell on the differences or offer an explanation for what went wrong.

What Sonia Gandhi leaves unsaid about Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan

Perhaps the most striking aspect of the memoir is how little space it gives to Amitabh Bachchan, considering his long association with Rajiv Gandhi and the Gandhi family.

According to a count in the book, Amitabh's name appears only three times. Jaya Bachchan, meanwhile, does not find a mention at all.

Sonia does recall Amitabh's presence during her early days in India and his friendship with Rajiv. But there is no substantial account of their relationship in the years that followed, his entry into politics, the Bofors controversy or the differences between the two families.

There is also no discussion of the relationship between the younger members of the two families or the public disagreements that emerged years later.

news.n_title: Once yearned for a home, SRK now has cyrotherapy, theatre at Mannat
news.n_description: Shah Rukh Khan recalled his journey from yearning for a home to owning Mannat, which boasts a cinema hall, cryotherapy facility and sea view. At a recent Dubai event, Karan Johar also credited Gauri Khan for the superstar's success.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Owning a house was once superstar Shah Rukh Khan’s biggest dream. Today, his Mumbai residence, Mannat, has a cinema hall, a cryotherapy facility and a sea view. At the launch of a luxury penthouse project named after him in Dubai, the actor reflected on his journey from having no home of his own to building a residence that draws crowds of fans.

Hosted by filmmaker Karan Johar, the event also featured his wife Gauri Khan, who designed the Dubai project. The conversation covered Shah Rukh’s early struggles, the personal meaning of Mannat, Gauri’s role in the family’s success and the values the couple want to pass on to their children, Aryan, Suhana and AbRam.

While introducing the project, Karan offered a glimpse of the features at Shah Rukh’s sea-facing Mumbai home. “Shah Rukh Khan’s Mannat has a cinema hall, cryotherapy and a sea view,” he said.

Karan also indicated that the Dubai project had drawn inspiration from several features of the actor’s residence.

At the event, Shah Rukh said owning a house had been one of his greatest dreams, particularly after losing his parents early in life and growing up without a home of his own.

“I come from a background where my parents died early,” he said. “It is not a sob story. This is how it was. I never had a house. My biggest yearning in life — of course, I love my films, family and work — but the only thing I love more than anything else is having a house.” - he added

The actor recalled that he did not own a house until he married Gauri. The couple bought their first home together, although the purchase was not easy. He said both that house and Mannat were beyond their financial means when they decided to buy them.

Shah Rukh said he believed that when people dream big and work towards their goals, life eventually finds a way to make them happen. He also shared an anecdote about his children teasing him over his wish to buy houses in different cities.

“They say, ‘Papa, we cannot buy a house everywhere.’ But I have been fortunate. God has been kind,” he said.

Why home matters to Shah Rukh

For the actor, a house is more than an investment or a symbol of success. “I have always been a big believer in home, a place to live in. Home is where you start from, and home is the nicest word in the universe. The word ‘home’ turns into an emotion. It becomes your identity, your pride and sometimes even your life,” he said.

Explaining why a home mattered so much to him, Shah Rukh added, “For me, it is very important. I often tell people that in life there are good days, bad days, sad days and sometimes even depressing days. But when you finally come knocking, you have to return to your own home because you regenerate there, figure things out again and go back to face the harsh world. So I am a big believer in having a house.”

He also had a message for people hoping to own their dream homes. “If you make a wish for a home, you will get the most beautiful home in life. Think big and believe big,” he said.

Gauri’s role in the family

Karan credited Gauri with playing a central role in the life Shah Rukh has built. Describing her as a pillar of support, he said: “I want everyone to know that there would be no Mannat and no Khan family if it were not for this pillar standing right next to me.”

He described Gauri as a form of Goddess Lakshmi and added, “Whosoever’s life she has touched, that life turns into gold.”

Shah Rukh also credited his wife with constantly encouraging him to dream bigger. He recalled that Gauri never viewed their early achievements as the finish line.

“Our first home, our first car, our first journey together — Gauri always said, ‘These are just the beginning. The first of many. And what we do next will be King style,’” he said.

Gauri has the final word at home

Gauri, who designed Mannat, said the process had been a cakewalk because she had the final say in every decision. “They have no option but to agree to all my designs,” she said.

Shah Rukh agreed, joking that nobody in the family was allowed to complain about anything related to the house, from the Wi-Fi and paintings to the lift.

“We cannot utter a word against Gauri’s house. We cannot complain about the Wi-Fi or the colour options, and neither are we allowed to eat in bed. We cannot talk about the paintings, terrace, chandelier, stairs or even the lift. We are just allowed to sit quietly and keep praising Gauri for her work. ‘Wow, Gauri, what a home you have made,’” he joked.

Lessons for Aryan, Suhana and AbRam

The conversation also turned to the values Shah Rukh wants to pass on to his children. Having received love and appreciation from audiences across generations, he said he wanted Aryan, Suhana and AbRam to understand the importance of good manners, dignity, humility and hard work.

He said success came from giving one’s best, regardless of the chosen field, and wanted his children to value the affection and appreciation they received instead of taking it for granted.

“Jokes apart, people have known me for years. There are different generations of people here who have appreciated my work, and I am extremely grateful and thankful to all of them,” he said. “The one thing I have learnt from this appreciation over the years is to teach my children good manners, dignity and, above all, humility. They should have the passion to give their best to whatever they do.”

He added, “If you give your best to whatever you do, there is no limit to what you can achieve because the love of the people is always there if you work hard. I just want them to be dignified, humble and hardworking.”

From Delhi to Mannat

Shah Rukh and Gauri bought their first home together in 1991 in Panchsheel Park, South Delhi. The actor initially owned the basement and first floor before eventually acquiring the remaining floors.

The couple later bought a sea-facing apartment in Mumbai before moving into Mannat in 2001. Over the years, fans have regularly gathered outside its gates to catch a glimpse of Shah Rukh. The property is currently being renovated, with Gauri adding extra floors.

The actor will be seen in the upcoming film King, which is slated to release on December 24. Directed by Siddharth Anand, the film also stars Deepika Padukone and Suhana Khan among others.

news.n_title: Cristiano Ronaldo kicks off new career beyond football, launches first TV series
news.n_description: Cristiano Ronaldo has taken his first step into television production, with filming beginning on his upcoming football drama series, Day 1s, which he is producing in partnership with British filmmaker Matthew Vaughn.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Cristiano Ronaldo is venturing into television production, with filming beginning on his first series, Day 1s, a football drama being developed in partnership with British filmmaker Matthew Vaughn.

The 41-year-old Portuguese superstar announced the development on Thursday, confirming that production had started on the project. Ronaldo will serve as an executive producer and is also expected to appear as himself in some episodes.

"Exciting news! Production of my first TV show, Day 1s, has just started. More to come!" Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.

Day 1s is among the first major projects from URMARV Studios, a production company co-founded by Ronaldo and Vaughn in April 2025. Vaughn, who has directed films such as Kick-Ass and Kingsman, has joined hands with the former Portugal captain to develop projects for film and television.

The series will explore the business side of football, with its story centered on Stanley Dalton, a British football agent played by actor Damian Lewis. The fictional character must navigate the pressures of the transfer market, where negotiations, player movements and commercial interests often shape the game away from the pitch.

Former Arsenal and France midfielder Thierry Henry will also feature in the series, playing himself. British rapper Dave is another member of the cast. The concept for the show comes from Darren Dein, the agent who represents Henry.

While Ronaldo's involvement as a producer has been confirmed, further details about his appearances and the series' release date are yet to be announced.

The project comes at an important moment in Ronaldo's playing career. He recently announced his retirement from international football, ending a 23-year association with Portugal. He made 234 appearances for his country, scoring a record 146 goals, and featured in six editions of the FIFA World Cup.

Ronaldo also captained Portugal to the European Championship title in 2016 and helped the team win the inaugural UEFA Nations League in 2019. His final appearance for the national side came in a 1-0 win over Wales on September 24.

Despite stepping away from international football, Ronaldo will continue playing at club level with Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr. He is currently on 985 career goals and remains in pursuit of the 1,000-goal milestone.

Meanwhile, Day 1s is not the only project in the pipeline for URMARV Studios. The company is also expected to unveil Stuntnuts, a film featuring Hollywood actors Matt Damon and Chris Hemsworth.

news.n_title: Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq cleared for domestic cricket as Pakistan probe nears end
news.n_description: Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq have been cleared to play domestic cricket as the NCCIA investigation into alleged dressing-room leaks nears its end. PCB chief Mohsin Naqvi expects the agency to submit its findings in the coming days.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi has confirmed that Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq have been cleared to play domestic cricket even as the investigation into alleged dressing-room leaks during the England tour approaches its conclusion.

The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) is investigating the two Pakistan players following the team's 0-3 Test series defeat against England. The inquiry centres on allegations that confidential information and internal matters from the dressing room were leaked during the tour.

Speaking to the media in Lahore on Thursday, Naqvi confirmed that both players had been given the go-ahead to feature in domestic cricket despite the ongoing investigation. He also indicated that the agency was close to completing its inquiry, although it needed further clarification from Rizwan before submitting its findings.

"I have spoken to the NCCIA and they just need more clarity from Rizwan, after which they will submit their findings in a few days' time, although I can't give an exact deadline," Naqvi said as quoted by PTI.

The PCB chairman's comments suggest that the investigation could reach a conclusion in the coming days. However, he stopped short of providing a fixed timeline for the report.

CENTRAL CONTRACTS TO BE ANNOUNCED SOON

Naqvi also addressed the delay in announcing Pakistan's central contracts, saying the process was close to completion and that the list would be made public soon.

"I think they are finalised or would be finalised by tomorrow," he added.

The PCB has delayed the announcement of its latest central contracts by around three months. The previous contracts expired on July 31, leaving players waiting for clarity on their revised terms.

NAQVI ADDRESSES PSL FINANCES

Naqvi was also asked about reports of financial constraints surrounding the Pakistan Super League (PSL). In response, he pointed to the amounts paid for the league's new franchises and the sale of Multan Sultans, arguing that franchise owners should have realistic expectations about returns on their investments.

"Whatever the owners of these new franchises know, they can't expect to make profits after a year or two, and they must have done their feasibility report before joining the PSL," he said.

The PCB chairman added that owners who wanted to sell their franchises at a profit were free to do so, provided they followed the league's rules and regulations.

NAQVI BACKS PAKISTAN'S CRICKET SET-UP

Naqvi also expressed confidence in the direction of Pakistan cricket, saying he trusted his team to manage cricketing matters and expected better results once the next group of young players was ready.

"I am there to back them all the time, and we are expecting much better results when the next batch of young players are ready in the next six months," he said.

news.n_title: India vs Pakistan in U19 Asia Cup final after Lakshya special blows away Afghanistan
news.n_description: India stormed into the U19 Asia Cup final with an eight-wicket thrashing of Afghanistan, powered by skipper Lakshya Raichandani's unbeaten 93. The win sets up a blockbuster clash against Pakistan on Saturday, with India eyeing revenge for their group-stage defeat and hoping to end their run of losing the last two finals.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Brief Scores: India U19 (230/2 in 36.5 overs) beat Afghanistan U19 (227/8 in 50 overs) by 8 wickets in Al Amerat.

India are set for another high-voltage showdown against Pakistan after booking their place in the Under-19 Asia Cup final with a commanding eight-wicket win over Afghanistan in Al Amerat on Thursday.

Skipper Lakshya Raichandani led from the front with a brilliant 93 off 90 balls as India chased down Afghanistan's 228-run target in just 36.5 overs. Aaryavir Sehwag also struck a half-century, helping India set up a blockbuster summit clash against their arch-rivals on Saturday.

India vs Afghanistan, U19 Asia Cup semifinal Highlights

Pakistan had earlier stormed into the final with a nine-wicket thrashing of Bangladesh. After bowling Bangladesh out for 138 in 31.4 overs, Pakistan completed the chase in just 21.5 overs, finishing at 141 for one. Hayam Khan top-scored with 69, while Usman Khan remained unbeaten on 64. Rizwanullah starred with the ball, claiming five wickets for 30 runs.

The final will be the second meeting between India and Pakistan in this year's tournament. India will be eager to settle scores after suffering a heartbreaking three-wicket defeat in their group-stage encounter on Diwali, when Hamza Zahoor struck an unbeaten century to snatch victory.

There is also unfinished business from last year's final, where Sameer Minhas' magnificent 171 powered Pakistan to the title. Having lost the 2024 final to Bangladesh and the 2025 summit clash to Pakistan, India will be desperate to end their recent final hoodoo and reclaim the crown.

Ishan Sood was particularly impressive, finishing with three wickets for 43 runs in nine overs. The spinners also kept things tight in the middle overs, with Yashbardhan Chauhan claiming one wicket for 26 runs in seven overs and Manal Chauhan conceding just 31 in his eight overs.

Aryan Savsani chipped in with two wickets, including the important dismissals of Amir Hamza and Tahir Sarwary, finishing with figures of 2 for 29. Arjun returned 1 for 20 in four overs, while Kavya Patel picked up one wicket for 38 runs. India's regular strikes and control in the middle overs ensured Afghanistan finished well short of their intended target.

LAKSHYA AND SEHWAG PUT INDIA IN CONTROL

India's chase got off to a commanding start, with Lakshya and Sehwag stitching together a 117-run opening partnership. While Sehwag took his time to settle in, the skipper set the tempo with an aggressive approach, finding the boundaries regularly and keeping the required run rate under control.

VINEETH HELPS INDIA SEAL THE FINAL SPOT

Lakshya continued the good work alongside No. 3 VK Vineeth. The duo kept the scoreboard moving, rotating the strike and punishing loose deliveries. Lakshya brought up his fifty and went on to make a fluent 93 off 90 balls, striking 13 fours and a six.

The captain looked set for a century but was unlucky to miss out in the 32nd over. Attempting to clear the infield against Sohail Khan, he failed to get enough elevation and was caught by Mohammad Ali at mid-off.

Vineeth ensured there were no further hiccups. He scored an unbeaten 57 off 62 balls, while Yashbardhan chipped in with 16 not out off 14 deliveries. Vineeth sealed the win in style, pulling Noor Ali Niazi for a six as India reached the target with 79 balls to spare.

news.n_title: Rishabh Pant declared fit, leaves for New Zealand to join Test squad
news.n_description: Rishabh Pant cleared a series of match simulation exercises at the BCCI Centre of Excellence and left for New Zealand, boosting India's preparations for the first Test, starting November 19, in Wellington.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant left for New Zealand on Thursday, November 12, after clearing a fitness test at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. In a major boost for the Shubman Gill-led Test side, Pant will be available for selection for the first Test, which begins on November 19.

Sources told India Today that Pant A pased a series of match simulation exercises, the last of which was on November 10. He left for New Zealand on Thursday morning and is scheduled to reach the country via Singapore.

Pant had been working hard on his rehabilitation at the CoE after a side strain, sustained during the Irani Cup in Srinagar in October, ruled him out of competitive action. He was initially named in India's A squad for the three unofficial Tests in New Zealand but was subsequently ruled out following the injury setback.

Pant had failed to clear his initial fitness test at the CoE on November 1. He was scheduled to undergo fresh assessments, including match simulations, on November 10, which he successfully completed.

The wicketkeeper-batter spent more than two weeks at the CoE, having arrived at the BCCI's world-class facility on October 23. His return to fitness comes as a significant boost for India ahead of a challenging two-Test series, although the team management will now have to work out a plan to get him acclimatised to New Zealand conditions without the benefit of a practice match.

Captain Shubman Gill, KL Rahul and Anshul Kamboj left the ongoing ODI series midway to join the Test squad in Wellington. Meanwhile, several of India's Test specialists, including Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Dhruv Jurel, Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja, featured in an unofficial Test against New Zealand A in Lincoln to get accustomed to the conditions.

The Test specialists, who will be overseen by bowling coach Morne Morkel and assistant coach Sitanshu Kotak, began training in Wellington on Thursday. Head coach Gautam Gambhir, meanwhile, will remain with the ODI squad for the final two matches of the series before joining the Test team.

Shreyas Iyer will lead India in the remaining two ODIs in Gill's absence, with the visitors holding a 2-0 lead in the three-match series.

BOTH PANT AND JUREL?

India will be hoping Pant is ready to slot straight into the playing XI for the first Test. However, his availability also presents the team management with a selection dilemma, with Dhruv Jurel having strengthened his case during the unofficial Test series against New Zealand A.

Jurel has been in India's playing XI alongside Pant in recent Test assignments, with the team finding ways to accommodate both wicketkeeper-batters. It remains to be seen whether the Rajasthan Royals star will once again feature as a specialist batter if Pant is selected as the first-choice wicketkeeper.

Jurel made a century and a half-century across four innings in the unofficial Test series, gaining valuable exposure to New Zealand conditions. His performances could make it difficult for the team management to leave him out, particularly after the preparation he has had in the country.

Pant, on the other hand, will have to quickly get accustomed to the conditions after arriving in New Zealand without any competitive match practice. He featured in two Tests during India's 2020 tour of New Zealand but endured a difficult outing, failing to cross the 25-run mark in any of his four innings.

news.n_title: Carrick sacked as Manchester United languish in Premier League relegation zone
news.n_description: Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick after a dismal start to the 2026-27 Premier League season left them 19th in the table. The club will now begin its search for a permanent successor after just one win in 10 matches.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Manchester United have parted ways with head coach Michael Carrick following a disappointing start to the 2026-27 Premier League season, bringing an end to his second spell at Old Trafford.

The decision comes after a difficult opening to the campaign, with United languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table after 10 matches. The Red Devils have managed just one victory during that period, leaving them facing an unexpected relegation battle and prompting the club hierarchy to make a change in the dugout.

United confirmed Carrick's departure in an official statement, thanking the former midfielder for his contribution to the club and acknowledging his achievements during his return last season.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," the statement read.

The club also confirmed that it intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible. However, no replacement has been announced, with the immediate focus likely to be on finding a candidate capable of turning around United's fortunes.

Carrick's departure marks a disappointing end to a tenure that had begun with considerable promise. Having returned to Manchester in January, the former England international initially took charge of the first team and made an immediate impact, guiding the club through an impressive run of results.

CARRICK'S PROMISING RETURN

Carrick rejoined United in January 2026 and helped revive their campaign after a difficult period. He guided the Red Devils to a third-place finish in the Premier League, winning 12 of their remaining 17 matches during the 2025-26 season.

United also accumulated the highest points tally in the league during that period, underlining the impact Carrick made after taking charge. His work in the dugout convinced the club to hand him the head coach's position on a permanent basis ahead of the new campaign.

The appointment was seen as an opportunity to build on the momentum generated during the closing months of the previous season. Carrick, who spent 12 years at Old Trafford as a player, was familiar with the club's expectations and had earned considerable goodwill among supporters.

However, the start of the 2026-27 campaign has been a different story altogether.

United have struggled to find consistency, with their lack of victories exposing problems at both ends of the pitch. Their position in 19th place after 10 matches has intensified the pressure on Carrick, with the club unwilling to allow the situation to deteriorate further.

The decision to part ways with the 45-year-old comes despite his impressive work last season, highlighting the urgency surrounding United's current predicament.

UNITED BEGIN SUCCESSOR SEARCH

In its statement, Manchester United were keen to acknowledge Carrick's contribution and his association with the club, describing him as a legend who had maintained the highest standards of dedication and professionalism.

"Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club," the statement added.

The club also expressed its appreciation for his leadership and achievements during the previous campaign, which helped United secure a top-three finish and return to the UEFA Champions League.

United now face an important decision over who takes charge of the first team. With the club sitting in the relegation zone, the next appointment will carry significant pressure, particularly with little room for a lengthy rebuilding process.

While Mauricio Pochettino has been linked with the managerial position, Manchester United have not officially confirmed an appointment or named their preferred candidate.

The Argentine has considerable Premier League experience from his time at Tottenham Hotspur and has also managed Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States men's national team.

For now, United's priority will be to identify a successor who can quickly restore confidence and get the team climbing the table. Having started the season with ambitions of challenging near the top, the immediate objective has shifted towards avoiding a prolonged battle against relegation.

Carrick leaves Old Trafford with the credit of having delivered an impressive turnaround last season, but his successor will inherit a club in need of an immediate response.
